row: The product keeps one list of the stores that hold graph content. For each store it says whether one graph's part can be kept apart there, and if not, why.

Graph.KG.GraphStores.Inventory(): one entry per store {name, kind sql or global, locator (the graph column or the subscript of the graph key), graphScoped, reason}. Scoped() and Unscoped() return the two halves (Unscoped keyed store, kind, reason for verification reports; GraphVerify.cls:169, 210); InventoryJSON() returns the list as JSON text for Python callers, since a %DynamicArray does not survive a Native API return. Not split by graph: rdf_reifications, ^NKG, ^KG("deg2p_exact_merged"), ^KG("labelset"), ^ArnoKG. Not on the list: ^EmbedQueue, docs_quarantine, edge_vector_quarantine, embedding_quarantine, the two rdf_edges rescue tables, the BM25 and vector indexes. Coverage (ontology-2): GraphStores.Inventory, GraphStores.Scoped, GraphStores.Unscoped, GraphStores.InventoryJSON.
A content check of one graph counts its entries in each store that keeps graphs apart, and gives a hash of them. It changes nothing.

GraphStores.Digest(graph) (spec 254): JSON {graph, stores: {name: {entries, sha256}}, skipped, empty}. Globals keyed at subscript 1 or 2: every node under the graph key in $Query order, as its subscripts below the key and its value (DigestGlobal). Tables: the graph's rows, columns in name order less the graph column, identity columns, created_at, updated_at and streams; row hashes are counted and walked sorted (DigestTable). ^IVG.Ledger("tuple") and ("stmt") go under skipped. It writes only the process-private ^||IVG.Digest. No product caller at the pin: the upstream e2e tests use it (tests/e2e/graph_snapshot.py:21). Coverage (ontology-2): GraphStores.Digest.
Two graphs that hold the same content get the same answer.
The graph key is not part of an entry. Coverage (ontology-2): GraphStores.Digest.
Erasing a list of edges removes those edges from one graph, with the statement entry of each. Their nodes stay.

Eraser.EraseEdges(graph, edgesJson), a JSON array of {s, p, o}: for each triple, every rdf_edges row of it in the graph with its reifications, kg_EdgeEmbeddings and edge-route rows (EraseEdgeRow), its ^KG adjacency (Adjacency.Remove, also when no row is behind it) and its live ("stmt") and ("tuple") entries. One transaction. When a row went or an adjacency entry existed it kills the graph's ^KG("deg2p") and ("deg2p_exact") and runs InvalidateDerived(1): ^NKG dropped, ^KG("__version") bumped, ^IVG.AlgoCache killed. Returns the rdf_edges rows removed. A payload that is not a JSON array is refused before the transaction. Callers: store.delete_edges (iris_sql_store.py:1474-1500) and the deprecated engine.bulk_delete_adjacency (nodes_edges.py:2335; WRT-B3.29, ADJ-B3.12). Coverage (ontology-2): EraseEdges.
Erasing everything empties every store on the list of stores, for all graphs at once. It keeps every ledger record.

Eraser.EraseAll, through engine.erase_all, which a replacing restore_snapshot runs first (module SNP). One transaction: every routed table emptied (claimed and orphan), the whole embedding_registry, every FHIR side table and watermark, rdf_reifications, labels, props, docs, both legacy vector tables, kg_EdgeEmbeddings, rdf_edges and nodes; Adjacency.RemoveAll, TemporalIndex.EraseAll; ^KG label, prop, labelset, deg2p, deg2p_exact and deg2p_exact_merged; ^NKG dropped and not marked for rebuild (InvalidateDerived(1, 0)); ^ArnoKG, ^IVG.GraphMode, ^IVG.TemporalStructural, ^IVG.AlgoCache, ^IVG.Ledger("stmt") and ("tuple"). Kept: ^IVG.Ledger("rec"), ^KG("__version") (bumped), ^NKG("$meta", "version"), Graph_KG.embedding_quarantine (Eraser.cls:753-758). Claimed routed tables are dropped after the commit (a failed drop leaves an empty table); orphans stay, empty. Coverage (ontology-2): EraseAll.
It returns how many rows of nodes and edges it removed. Zero means there were none.
The test erases everything twice; the second call returns 0. Coverage (ontology-2): EraseAll.
Erasing a list of edges, or everything, takes no ledger lock. So a commit does not wait for it.

As for a graph erasure (ERS-T2, F-1201): EraseEdges kills each edge's live ("stmt") and ("tuple") entries (EraseEdgeRow, Eraser.cls:667-678) and EraseAll kills both trees (Eraser.cls:810-811), each in its own transaction with no Lock on ^IVG.Ledger("head"). F-1114 saw the EraseEdges path live, reached from bulk_delete_adjacency. Coverage (ontology-2): EraseEdges, EraseAll.
A sweep of one graph removes the nodes that hold nothing: no edge, label, property, document or vector.

Eraser.EraseBareNodes(graph, batch, dryRun, minAgeSec), called by store and engine erase_bare_nodes (strict mode is checked there, TMP-B12.8; no ledger record is written). The test is BareClauses: no rdf_edges row either way, no rdf_labels, rdf_props or docs row, no row in either legacy vector table or a routed node table, all in the node's own graph; a node with a ^KG("out") or ("in") entry is kept too. The same id in another graph is untouched. A node that create_node made keeps its id property, so it is never swept (upstream test test_a_node_create_node_made_keeps_its_id_property_and_so_survives_both_the_purge_and_the_sweep). Removed nodes lose their derived entries (ForgetNodes: Adjacency.RemoveSource, ^KG("prop")); then InvalidateDerived(0): ^NKG kept, ^KG("__version") bumped. Returns JSON {graph, bare, erased, kept, batches, dry_run}. The purges' retirement runs the same delete on the ids they name (module TMP). Coverage (ontology-2): EraseBareNodes.
A dry run only counts those nodes. It changes nothing.
pDryRun=1: one SELECT COUNT(*) with the same clauses; no row, no global, not ^KG("__version"). The test compares every graph-scoped store by GraphStores.Digest. Coverage (ontology-2): EraseBareNodes.
A node that gains an edge, a label or a vector while the sweep runs is kept.

The DELETE carries every test again, and the foreign keys of edges, labels and the vector tables refuse it (SQLCODE -124, counted kept), even for a dependant not yet committed. Properties and documents have no foreign key: a property or document written after the DELETE has looked can be left with no node (Eraser.cls:1197-1201, an orphan property in module WRT's terms). pMinAgeSec keeps the sweep off nodes made in the last given seconds (upstream test test_the_sweep_leaves_a_node_younger_than_the_minimum_age). Coverage (ontology-2): EraseBareNodes.
Each batch of the sweep is saved on its own. A failure undoes only the batch it was in.

DeleteBareSet: a transaction commits after pBatch removed nodes (default 10,000) or at the end, then ForgetNodes runs for that batch. A named exception to SYS-I4: earlier batches stay removed, and running the sweep again finishes. Coverage (ontology-2): EraseBareNodes.
A graph erasure or a node erasure leaves the queued embedding requests of the erased nodes in place. So does erasing everything.

Read: EraseGraph, EraseIdSet (the body of EraseNodes and EraseNodeIds) and EraseAll. ^EmbedQueue(reqId, "text" | "node_id" | "result" | "graph" | ...), reqId the node id or txt:<n>, holds the text to embed and the result vector. Only EmbedQueue.ClearDone removes entries, and only DONE ones; PENDING and ERROR stay. No line of Eraser.cls names ^EmbedQueue, and GraphStores.Inventory does not list it. Reach obligation REACH-1 (review R2-10); whether it should be reached or named is a maintainer question (STATUS residual question 1). Coverage (ontology-2): EraseIdSet (by its cited lines); reach obligation REACH-1.
A graph erasure or a node erasure leaves the table of documents that an upgrade could not place in a graph. So does erasing everything.

Read: EraseGraph, EraseIdSet (the body of EraseNodes and EraseNodeIds) and EraseAll. Graph_KG.docs_quarantine (doc_id, text, reason, quarantined_at), with no graph column: the docs migration moves each row it cannot place there, text included. No product path deletes from it; Eraser.cls never names it and GraphStores.Inventory does not list it. Graph_KG.embedding_quarantine is the same kind of store (F-C1305). Reach obligation REACH-2; whether it should be reached or named is a maintainer question (STATUS residual question 1). Coverage (ontology-2): reach obligation REACH-2 (no entry point of its own).
A graph erasure or a node erasure leaves the table of vectors of edges that an upgrade could not place in a graph. So does erasing everything.

Read: EraseGraph, EraseIdSet (the body of EraseNodes and EraseNodeIds) and EraseAll. Graph_KG.edge_vector_quarantine (s, p, o_id, reason, emb, quarantined_at), with no graph column: the edge-vector migration puts there each kg_EdgeEmbeddings row with no edge, or with no graph it could choose (edge_quarantine_no_edge, edge_quarantine_by_key). No product path deletes from it; Eraser.cls never names it and GraphStores.Inventory does not list it. Reach obligation REACH-3; whether it should be reached or named is a maintainer question (STATUS residual question 1). Coverage (ontology-2): reach obligation REACH-3 (no entry point of its own).
A graph erasure or a node erasure only marks the saved copy of the default graph as old. The copy stays until one of the three calls that read it builds a new one. Erasing everything removes it.

^ArnoKG("KG", "graph_json") holds the default graph's node ids and edges, read from ^KG("out") (BuildGraphJson), and ("version") the ^KG("__version") it was built at. InvalidateDerived bumps ^KG("__version") (ArnoAccel.BumpVersion); CacheGraphJson rebuilds the copy when the two differ, and only KhopSampleJson, RandomWalkJson and NeighborAggJson call it, in USER only. Until then the copy keeps the erased ids. EraseAll kills ^ArnoKG (Eraser.cls:806). GraphStores lists it as not split by graph (GraphStores.cls:131). Reach obligation REACH-4; whether it should be reached or named is a maintainer question (STATUS residual question 1). Coverage (ontology-2): InvalidateDerived; reach obligation REACH-4.
A graph erasure or a node erasure leaves the two tables where an upgrade from version 3.2 kept copies of edges. So does erasing everything.

Read: EraseGraph, EraseIdSet (the body of EraseNodes and EraseNodeIds) and EraseAll. Graph_KG.rdf_edges__ivg400rescue (s, p, o_id, qualifiers, graph_id): initialize_schema copies a 3.2.0 class-owned rdf_edges there, restores from it and drops it only when every row is placed (schema.py:3259); a failed restore leaves it. Graph_KG.rdf_edges__ivg400unplaced keeps the rows that could not go back, for the operator. Neither Eraser.cls nor GraphStores.cls names them. Reach obligation REACH-5; whether it should be reached or named is a maintainer question (STATUS residual question 1). Coverage (ontology-2): reach obligation REACH-5 (no entry point of its own).
A caller can ask whether a redaction run is not done. The answer gives a hash of the target, its start time and who started it, but not the target.

LedgerRedact.InProgress() returns {ok, in_progress[, target_sha256, started_ms, actor]} from ^IVG.Ledger("redacting"); the marker's graph and match (LedgerRedact.cls:20) are not returned. GraphLedger.redaction_in_progress() returns that object, or None when there is no marker. The record readers' refusal (client.py:687-693) and verify (replay.py:812) ask it. Coverage (ontology-2): LedgerRedact.InProgress, redaction_in_progress.
A redaction run leaves the queued embedding requests alone. Its redaction receipt does not list them as out of reach.

^EmbedQueue keeps the text, node id, vector and graph of PENDING and ERROR entries. The receipt's out_of_reach names earlier exports, IRIS journals and backups only (LedgerRedact.cls:505-509). Redaction writes only the ledger's own globals and tables (^IVG.Ledger, ledger_revisions, the audit revision); no line of LedgerRedact.cls names this store. Reach obligation REACH-1 (review R2-10); whether it should be reached or named is a maintainer question (STATUS residual question 1). Coverage (ontology-2): reach obligation REACH-1 (no entry point of its own).
A redaction run leaves the table of documents that an upgrade could not place in a graph. Its redaction receipt does not list that table as out of reach.

Graph_KG.docs_quarantine keeps the document id and text. The receipt's out_of_reach names earlier exports, IRIS journals and backups only (LedgerRedact.cls:505-509). Redaction writes only the ledger's own globals and tables (^IVG.Ledger, ledger_revisions, the audit revision); no line of LedgerRedact.cls names this store. Reach obligation REACH-2; whether it should be reached or named is a maintainer question (STATUS residual question 1). Coverage (ontology-2): reach obligation REACH-2 (no entry point of its own).
A redaction run leaves the table of vectors of edges that an upgrade could not place in a graph. Its redaction receipt does not list that table as out of reach.

Graph_KG.edge_vector_quarantine keeps each edge's s, p, o_id and vector. The receipt's out_of_reach names earlier exports, IRIS journals and backups only (LedgerRedact.cls:505-509). Redaction writes only the ledger's own globals and tables (^IVG.Ledger, ledger_revisions, the audit revision); no line of LedgerRedact.cls names this store. Reach obligation REACH-3; whether it should be reached or named is a maintainer question (STATUS residual question 1). Coverage (ontology-2): reach obligation REACH-3 (no entry point of its own).
A redaction run does not touch the saved copy of the default graph. Its redaction receipt does not list that copy as out of reach.

^ArnoKG("KG") holds the default graph's node ids and edges. A redaction does not bump ^KG("__version"), so a copy built before the erasure that no sampling call has rebuilt still holds the erased ids afterwards (ERS module, ERS-B98). The receipt's out_of_reach names earlier exports, IRIS journals and backups only (LedgerRedact.cls:505-509). Redaction writes only the ledger's own globals and tables (^IVG.Ledger, ledger_revisions, the audit revision); no line of LedgerRedact.cls names this store. Reach obligation REACH-4; whether it should be reached or named is a maintainer question (STATUS residual question 1). Coverage (ontology-2): reach obligation REACH-4 (no entry point of its own).
A redaction run leaves the two tables where an upgrade from version 3.2 kept copies of edges. Its redaction receipt does not list them as out of reach.

Graph_KG.rdf_edges__ivg400rescue and rdf_edges__ivg400unplaced keep s, p, o_id, qualifiers and graph_id. The receipt's out_of_reach names earlier exports, IRIS journals and backups only (LedgerRedact.cls:505-509). Redaction writes only the ledger's own globals and tables (^IVG.Ledger, ledger_revisions, the audit revision); no line of LedgerRedact.cls names this store. Reach obligation REACH-5; whether it should be reached or named is a maintainer question (STATUS residual question 1). Coverage (ontology-2): reach obligation REACH-5 (no entry point of its own).
The report it gives then is not marked equal.
VerificationReport.equal is result == "equal"; the result is then redaction_in_progress, so equal is False, as for diverges. Coverage (ontology-2): VerificationReport.equal.
A tombstone row becomes a record marked redacted. It keeps only its place, flags and hash, and the kinds of change and item it replaced.

MutationRecord.from_row on a ledger_records row: op "redacted", entity_kind the replaced record's, entity_id and attr "", prior, new and graph None, flags, digest, redacted_op. MutationRecord.redacted is op == "redacted". Coverage (ontology-2): MutationRecord.redacted, MutationRecord.from_row.
Rows from a server older than redaction, which have no hash columns, still read as records.
12 columns before spec 256, 14 since (digest, redacted_op); a 12-column row gets digest and redacted_op None. Coverage (ontology-2): MutationRecord.from_row.
A record turns into plain fields and back without change. Only a tombstone's fields hold a hash and the kind of change it replaced.

MutationRecord.to_wire and MutationRecord.from_wire: seq, ordinal, op, entity_kind, entity_id, attr, prior, new, graph, flags, plus digest and redacted_op for a tombstone. Coverage (ontology-2): MutationRecord.to_wire, MutationRecord.from_wire.
Record readers and the verify call read records in order, in pages of at most 5,000.

iter_records_sql pages Graph_KG.ledger_records(seqFrom, seqTo, ordinalFrom, pageSize) with RECORD_PAGE 5,000, and iter_records joins the pages in (seq, ordinal) order and stops past seqTo. Each page is its own query, with no lock between them (see RPL-I1). Used by get_revision, diff, reconstruct, export_reconstruction (client.py:695-739) and verify (replay.py:825). Coverage (ontology-2): iter_records, iter_records_sql.
Each record has one fixed text form: its fields as JSON, with the keys in name order. A tombstone's form holds only its hash, flags, place and the change it replaced.

Ledger.CanonicalRecord(seq, ordinal) (R14): attr, entity_id, entity_kind, flags as an array, graph (null when empty), new and prior (null when absent), op, ordinal, seq; "" when there is no such record. A tombstone: digest, flags, op "redacted", ordinal, redacted_op, seq. A redaction hashes this form into the tombstone (LedgerRedact.cls:335, module RED). Coverage (ontology-2): Ledger.CanonicalRecord.
An export of a rebuilt graph writes one line of JSON for each node, then one for each edge, in a fixed order. It says how many of each it wrote.

export_ndjson(state, path), called by GraphLedger.export_reconstruction: node lines {type, id, labels, props}, edge lines {type, s, p, o, graph, quals, stmt_id}; nodes sorted by id, edges by (s, p, o, graph, statement id); keys sorted, non-ASCII kept. It opens the path for writing, so a file already there is replaced. Returns ExportSummary(path, nodes, rels). Coverage (ontology-2): export_ndjson.
A diff gives the net change of each node and edge between two revisions. An item made and removed in between leaves no entry.

compute_diff over the records after the first revision up to the second (GraphLedger.diff). Entries: attr "" for existence, label:<name>, prop:<key>, qual:<key>, with before and after; an attribute that ends where it started gives none. Tombstones give no entry and are listed in Diff.redacted (RPL-B5). Coverage (ontology-2): compute_diff.
An item removed and then made again in between shows as two entries, one for each.
FR-029, FR-029a: a removal entry for the first life and a creation entry for the second, with the second life's attributes. Coverage (ontology-2): compute_diff.
Entries come in a fixed order: nodes first, then edges, each by id and then by field.
_sort_key: (0 for node, 1 for rel, entity_id, attr). Coverage (ontology-2): compute_diff.
A diff asked from a later revision back to an earlier one is the forward diff turned around. Each entry swaps its before and after.

GraphLedger.diff(a, b) with a after b returns compute_diff(b..a).inverse(): Diff.inverse sorts the swapped entries and keeps the redacted list; DiffEntry.inverse swaps before and after. Coverage (ontology-2): DiffEntry.inverse, Diff.inverse.
A diff can be given as a plain list. Each entry names the item, the field, and the value before and after.
Diff.to_list: one DiffEntry.to_wire dict per entry {entity_kind, entity_id, attr, before, after}; the redacted list is not in it. Coverage (ontology-2): Diff.to_list, DiffEntry.to_wire.
An entry for an edge that was made or removed also gives the edge's two ends, its type and its graph. A node entry gives none.

DiffEntry.rel_info parses after, or before when after is None, as JSON {s, p, o, graph}; None for a node entry, when both are None or when the text is not JSON. It is not in the plain list (test_to_wire_unchanged_no_rel_info_key). On a qualifier entry (attr qual:<key>) it parses the qualifier's value instead, so it can return a number, a boolean or another object, not the edge. Coverage (ontology-2): DiffEntry.rel_info.
A handle on a text index runs the engine's BM25 build, search, insert, drop and info for its own name.

Index(type="fulltext"); engine.index(name) maps the registry type bm25 to fulltext (_LEGACY_TO_CONCEPT). build -> _build_fulltext_index (vector.py:299-310) -> bm25_build; search -> bm25_search(name, q, k); insert -> bm25_insert(name, id, text); drop -> bm25_drop, then _index_registry.pop(name); info -> bm25_info unchanged. The handle in general is module OPS's (OPS-D16, OPS-B8). Coverage (ontology-2): Index.build[fulltext], Index.search[fulltext], Index.insert[fulltext], Index.drop[fulltext], Index.info[fulltext].
A handle build takes the property names from the call, then from the handle's setup. With neither, it indexes only the name property.

props = kw["properties"] or cfg.properties (FulltextIndexConfig, at least one) or ["name"]; k1 and b come from the call, then the setup, else 1.5 and 0.75. A handle with no setup (an index found when the engine started, or one made by bm25_build) has cfg None, so build() with no arguments rebuilds that index over name alone: the index keeps no list of its properties (^BM25Idx(name,"cfg") holds k1, b, N, graph, schema and counters). bm25_build drops the old index first (TXT-B1.1); zero documents then raise IndexNotBuiltError (TXT-X2). Coverage (ontology-2): Index.build[fulltext].
A handle build with no graph in the call builds for the default graph. A text setup cannot name a graph.

graph = kw.get("graph", getattr(cfg, "graph", None)); FulltextIndexConfig has no graph field and forbids extra keys, so it gives None and bm25_build uses DEFAULT_GRAPH. The graph an existing index saved (^BM25Idx(name,"cfg","graph"), TXT-D9) is not read, so a handle rebuild of another graph's index moves it to the default graph. Coverage (ontology-2): Index.build[fulltext].
A handle search is refused when the index is missing or has no documents. The engine's own search gives an empty list then.

search() calls status(), which reads info(): bm25_info gives N (only type when there is no index), _rows_of takes N, and 0 rows is state empty, so IndexNotBuiltError is raised before bm25_search runs. This costs one extra Info call per search. Contrast TXT-B2.10 and TXT-B2.11 (the engine call answers []). The refusal for every handle type is OPS-X8.1. Coverage (ontology-2): Index.search[fulltext].
A handle search passes on only the query and k. Any other option, such as the cutoff, is dropped.

_SEARCH["fulltext"] calls e.bm25_search(name, q, k) and ignores **kwargs, so max_df_fraction and report=True cannot be used through a handle, and an unknown option is not an error. Coverage (ontology-2): Index.search[fulltext].
A handle insert takes the text where a vector would go. It gives back nothing, so a text with no words looks like any other.

Index.insert(id, vector) calls bm25_insert(name, id, vector) and drops its bool (False when the text has no words, TXT-B4.7). The refusals of TXT-X5 to TXT-X7 still raise. Coverage (ontology-2): Index.insert[fulltext].
A handle drop deletes the index and its data. Then it takes the name off the engine's list.

bm25_drop (Kill ^BM25Idx(name), TXT-B7 and TXT-B7.1), then _index_registry.pop(name). The engine's _index_graph_scopes and _pending_index_config keep the name. Coverage (ontology-2): Index.drop[fulltext].
Registering a text index setup with replace, on a name the engine knows, drops the old index and its data at once. Nothing is built until the handle's build runs.

Coverage (ontology-2): ReconstructionTooLargeError.__init__.
The SQL form adds a zero row for each node of the graph that the walk left unscored. These rows come after the scored rows, in id order, up to the row limit.

PageRank.WithUnscored(pJson, pSchema, pGraph, pLimit), called by the kg_PPR SQL function behind CALL ivg.ppr: reads <schema>.nodes WHERE graph_id = COALESCE(?, '') ORDER BY node_id and stops once pLimit rows are filled; an answer with no row, or with pLimit rows already, is returned unread; an SQL error throws. The Python methods add the same rows themselves (ALG-B2.6). Coverage (ontology-2): PageRank.WithUnscored.
An older PageRank class is still installed where the server has embedded Python. It reads the nodes and edges of every graph whose ids match a pattern, so its scores mix graphs.

Graph.KG.PageRankEmbedded.ComputePageRank and ComputePageRankWithMetrics (embedded Python) over ComputePageRankCore: SELECT ... FROM nodes / rdf_edges WHERE node_id LIKE ?, unqualified table names, no graph_id (F-1013). No engine method calls it; setup deploys it where embedded Python exists. Coverage (ontology-2): PageRankEmbedded.ComputePageRank, PageRankEmbedded.ComputePageRankWithMetrics.
On the server, closeness reads the interned snapshot along out-edges, in-edges or both, up to a hop limit. It uses the same two formulas as the engine method.

NKGAccelCentrality.ClosenessGlobal (a BFS from each node) and ClosenessGlobalMSBFS (every source at once over bit sets) give the same scores: harmonic is the sum of 1/d; classical is reached / sum of d when reached = n - 1, else 0, n the nodes the snapshot holds; ranked by score then id and cut to topK (RankedJson). Both run EnsureNKG first. Reached through NKGAccel by the store's closeness tier (only while no named graph has an edge, ALG-B5.19) and by kg_Closeness. Coverage (ontology-2): NKGAccelCentrality.ClosenessGlobal, NKGAccelCentrality.ClosenessGlobalMSBFS, NKGAccel.ClosenessGlobal, NKGAccel.ClosenessGlobalMSBFS.
On the server, betweenness scores the directed graph for out and in, and the undirected graph for both. It takes its sample in the same fixed hashed order as the engine.

NKGAccelCentrality.BetweennessGlobal is BetweennessGlobalParallel with numJobs 0. Sources: sampleSize when 0 < sampleSize < n, else maxSources (200) when below n, else all n; scale n / sources, halved for both; first 7 bytes of the SHA-1 of the UTF-8 id, then the id (4.6.0 R233); in reads the out-edge bits (reversing every edge leaves betweenness unchanged); a node scoring 0 has no row; ranked, then cut to topK. The store's tier 1 passes maxSources = sample_size when one is named. Coverage (ontology-2): NKGAccelCentrality.BetweennessGlobal, NKGAccelCentrality.BetweennessGlobalParallel, NKGAccel.BetweennessGlobal, NKGAccel.BetweennessGlobalParallel.

Server betweenness splits its start nodes over background jobs: as many as the caller asks, else one per processor up to eight. The jobs share work areas kept under the caller's process number, which the run clears at its end. Areas left by a process that has gone are cleared too.

^bcParSrc(pid), ^bcParScore(pid, job, node) and ^bcBitAdj(pid) are globals because %SYSTEM.WorkMgr runs BetweennessWorker in other processes (4.6.0 R136); numJobs 0 is the CPU count capped at 8; a positive numJobs is used as given, capped at the source count. BetweennessWorker, called on its own, reads its sources from ^bcParSrc(parentPid) and adds to ^bcParScore(parentPid, workerN) only; a failed queue or job answers 'ERROR:...' after clearing. Coverage (ontology-2): NKGAccelCentrality.BetweennessWorker, NKGAccel.BetweennessWorker.

On the server, neighbourhood betweenness takes the nodes within some hops of a start node along out-edges. It scores the directed paths inside that set. A start node that is not in the snapshot gives an error text.

NKGAccelCentrality.BetweennessNeighborhood: EnsureNKG; the k-hop walk over ^NKG(-1) with a 1,000,000-node limit; directed Brandes in WorkMgr jobs on the induced out-edges (4.6.0 R050); zeros left out; ranked, cut to topK (20); 'ERROR:seed node not found: ...'. The store calls it through NKGAccel only while no named graph has an edge (ALG-B5.15). Coverage (ontology-2): NKGAccelCentrality.BetweennessNeighborhood, NKGAccel.BetweennessNeighborhood.

The server's closeness and betweenness refuse a direction other than out, in or both. Betweenness also refuses a hop limit that is not a whole number of zero or more. Each refusal is an error text with no scores.

Answers 'ERROR:direction must be out, in or both, not ...' and 'ERROR:maxHops must be a whole number 0 or more, not ...' (4.6.0 round 3; before, any other value walked out). The kg_Betweenness and kg_Closeness SQL functions throw IVG 5001 on an ERROR: answer. Coverage (ontology-2): the refusals of the server closeness and betweenness methods.

A further closeness method on the server uses an optional Python graph library. No engine path calls it. It treats each edge as two-way, and without the library it gives a marker text instead of scores.

Communities.ClosenessJsonPy(formula, topK): igraph closeness(mode=all, normalized) or harmonic_centrality(mode=all) * (n - 1) over the snapshot's out rows made two-way, self-loops dropped, every graph merged; 'PYUNAVAIL' without igraph; 'ERROR:^NKG not built'. The store's _closeness_serverside wraps it, and nothing calls that. Coverage (ontology-2): Communities.ClosenessJsonPy.

CALL ivg.degreeCentrality({direction, predicate, topK}) YIELD node, score, degree: one kg_DegreeCentrality branch per graph of _procedure_graphs (the USE GRAPH graph, else every graph with an edge), rows tagged with graph_id (4.6.0 R163, R192); options through DegreeCentralityInput (_procedure_options); an unknown key is a ValueError listing the allowed ones. Coverage (ontology-2): ivg.degreecentrality.

Communities.KCoreJson(topK): EnsureNKG, BuildSymAdj over ^NKG(-1), Batagelj-Zaversnik peeling; ^NKG holds every graph merged; a node with no edge has no row; 'ERROR:^NKG not built'. Communities.LeidenJsonPy(gamma, topK, randomSeed): leidenalg ModularityVertexPartition at gamma 1, else CPMVertexPartition; edges made two-way, self-loops dropped, every graph merged; 'PYUNAVAIL' without igraph or leidenalg, and LeidenJsonAuto then runs LeidenJson. IRISGraphStore.execute_scc and execute_k_core: _scc_arno / _k_core_arno unless IVG_DISABLE_ARNO=1, then _scc_lazykg / _k_core_lazykg over the default graph's ^KG (ALG-B6.6); an ArnoError falls back silently, any other exception with a warning. Before the store calls the Arno library over SQL, it checks the library once in each database session. That check first creates the bridge's SQL functions, so a read can change the schema. arno_available(conn, schema): IVG_DISABLE_ARNO=1 answers False; record_configured_lib_path loads IVG_ARNO_LIB on the server (ArnoAccel.Load records ^ArnoAccel("lib_path")) when the server resolves another path; resolve_lib_path is IVG_ARNO_LIB, else ArnoAccel.LibPath, else the default path; _ensure_zf_call_function creates the ivg_arno_zf_* wrappers the routine record lacks and commits (refused at $TLEVEL > 0, which the probe catches as False); then SELECT ivg_arno_zf_probe(lib, 'version'); the answer and path are kept per connection id. Called by the store's triangle, SCC, k-core and Leiden library paths, which fall back on ArnoError. Coverage (ontology-2): arno_call.

Coverage (ontology-2): ivg.closeness, ivg.eigenvector, ivg.leiden, ivg.trianglecount, ivg.scc.

The server's own guided subgraph runs its own PageRank over the default graph's out-edges. It keeps the best nodes, then walks out from them, holding at most twice the top count of nodes. A start list that cannot be read gives an empty answer.

Subgraph.PPRGuidedJson(seedJson, alpha 0.15 = teleport, eps 1e-5, topK 50, maxHops 5, edgeTypesJson): up to 50 rounds, stopping below 1e-4 after round 2; a node with no out-edge keeps only alpha of its score; start nodes are not checked against the node table; kept nodes score at least eps * max, at most topK; the walk caps at 2 * topK nodes and still lists an edge to a node past the cap. No engine method calls it (kg_PPR_GUIDED_SUBGRAPH runs in Python, ALG-B8.8). Coverage (ontology-2): Subgraph.PPRGuidedJson.

Coverage (ontology-2): TraversalBFS.BFSJSON, TraversalBFS.BFSFastJsonDirect, TraversalBFS.BFSFastCountDistinct and their Traversal delegators.

Coverage (ontology-2): TraversalBFS.BFSFastJsonChunked, ReadBFSChunk, BFSFastStream, the part reader, ReadBFSResultsStream and their Traversal delegators.

^ArnoKG("bfs_chunk", tag, n), the tag made from $Now and $Random, not the process: a part never read stays in the database. ^||BFS.Out("S", n) is process-private. Coverage (ontology-2): the staging areas of BFSFastJsonChunked and BFSFastStream.

Coverage (ontology-2): TraversalBFS.ReadBFSPage, Traversal.ReadBFSPage.

The one-hop count gives a node's out-edge count in the default graph, for one edge type or all. It may keep that count for later calls. The one-hop list gives the far end of each such edge, one line per edge.

Coverage (ontology-2): TraversalKHop.KHopCount, TraversalKHop.KHopNeighborIds and their Traversal delegators.

The fast and exact two-hop counts walk with KHop2Count when their stored count is not current (ALG-B9.12). Coverage (ontology-2): TraversalKHop.KHop2Count, TraversalKHop.KHop2NeighborIds and their Traversal delegators.

The snapshot exports list the snapshot's out-edges, so they mix every graph's edges. A large export is staged in parts inside the caller's process. With no snapshot, the plain export gives an empty text.

NKGAccelAdjacency.ExportAdjacency: "" unless UseNKG, then node-number lines 'src:dst,...' after a NODEMAP part, always staged in ^||adj and answered 'CHUNKED:<n>|NODEMAP' ("" with no rows); the NKGAccel doc's 'string directly if < 3MB' is not what it does. ExportAdjacencyWithPreds(requiredPreds, pMaxChars): 'src US type US dst' lines by id, 'OVERSIZE' past pMaxChars, staged in ^||adjWP past 3,000,000 characters ('CHUNKED:<n>'); the library walk calls it with its size cap (ALG-B9.8). Coverage (ontology-2): NKGAccelAdjacency.ExportAdjacency, NKGAccelAdjacency.ExportAdjacencyWithPreds, NKGAccel.ExportAdjacency.
A snapshot walk answer over 9,000 characters is handed over in parts kept in the caller's process. Reading a part leaves it in place until the next answer under the same name.

NKGAccelAdjacency.StoreLargeOut(tag, json): 'CHUNKED:<tag>:<n>' over ^||LargeOut(tag, n), killed first; the k-hop text form ("KHOP") and RandomWalkJson ("RW") use it. Its part reader reads ^||LargeOut without killing it; the tag "BFS" reads the library's shared reply ^ArnoKG("bfs_result", n) instead. Coverage (ontology-2): NKGAccelAdjacency.StoreLargeOut and its part reader, and the NKGAccel delegator.
The sorted k-hop form stages the nodes it reached in the shared walk work area under a tag. The reader lists them by distance and then node id, and then removes them.

NKGAccelTraversal.KHopNeighborsSorted answers 'SORTED:<tag>:<count>:<seed>:<k>' over ^ArnoKG("khop_r", tag, dist, node), the start node at distance 0, or 'SORTED:0' for a start node ^NKG lacks. NKGAccelAdjacency.ReadKHopResults gives the comma-joined {"id","dist"} rows and kills the tag; host._decode_sorted wraps them. Coverage (ontology-2): NKGAccelTraversal.KHopNeighborsSorted, NKGAccelAdjacency.ReadKHopResults and their NKGAccel delegators.

The snapshot k-hop walk lists the nodes within some hops of a start node along out-edges, each with its distance. It stops at a node limit, 1,000 by default, and mixes every graph's edges. A start node not in the snapshot gives an error object.

NKGAccelTraversal.KHopNeighbors(seedId, k 2, maxNodes 1000): {"seed","hops","totalNodes","nodes":[{"id","dist"}]}, the start node at 0; ids escaped (4.6.0 R306); no EnsureNKG, so a marked snapshot is read as it is; where ^NKG("$meta") is absent it reads the old ^KG("out", node, ...) layout, which production does not write, and lists the start node alone. KHopJson stages the same text through StoreLargeOut("KHOP"). Coverage (ontology-2): NKGAccelTraversal.KHopNeighbors, NKGAccelTraversal.KHopJson and their NKGAccel delegators.
Three reads tell how the last library walk in this process went. They give the path it took, the error behind a fall back, and the number of parts its reply came in.

NKGAccelTraversal.LastBfsPath ("native", "size-gate", "fallback" or ""; a walk with no library leaves it as it was), LastBfsError, LastBfsChunks, from ^||NKGAccel; process-private, for tests and diagnostics; they change nothing. Coverage (ontology-2): NKGAccelTraversal.LastBfsPath, NKGAccelTraversal.LastBfsError, NKGAccelTraversal.LastBfsChunks.

The snapshot path search gives the hop count of a shortest path along edge direction, or minus one when it finds none. It searches from both ends, each up to the hop limit, so it can find a path up to twice that long.

NKGAccelTraversal.ShortestPathNKG(srcId, dstId, maxHops 10): {"hops": n}; forward over ^NKG(-1), backward over ^NKG(-2), every graph merged, no edge-type filter; an empty or unknown id gives -1, the same node 0; with maxHops 1 a two-hop path answers 2. No product caller (scripts/bench/alt/suites.py names it). Coverage (ontology-2): NKGAccelTraversal.ShortestPathNKG, NKGAccel.ShortestPathNKG.

The distinct count walks the snapshot to one hop short of the limit. It then joins the stored sketches of the out-neighbours of each node it reached. So the count is an estimate, and it mixes every graph's edges.

NKGAccelTraversal.CountDistinctKHop(srcId, predsJson, maxHops 2, direction both): expands maxHops - 1 hops over ^NKG(-1)/(-2) by the direction, keeping every node reached (the start too), then merges ^NKG("$agg", node, type, "hll") of the listed types or of all; {"estimate","registers":256,"std_error":0.065}; a start node not interned answers estimate 0 with the note "node not found". The sketches hold out-neighbours only, so query.py sends only outgoing walks here (4495). Coverage (ontology-2): NKGAccelTraversal.CountDistinctKHop, NKGAccel.CountDistinctKHop.

The neighbour procedure lists the nodes one hop from the given sources, along one edge type if named. It gives one row for each graph and neighbour, and a query that names a graph reads only that graph's edges. A direction other than out, in or both is refused.

CALL ivg.neighbors(sources, predicate, direction) YIELD neighbor: SELECT DISTINCT over rdf_edges, tagged with COALESCE(graph_id, '') (4.6.0 R192); a source that is not a string or list, a predicate that is not a string, or an options map is refused (ValueError). Coverage (ontology-2): ivg.neighbors.
A list of edge types that cannot be read counts as no list, so the walk follows every type.

Every string form (Json, JsonDirect, JsonChunked, Stream, JsonSorted, CountDistinct) parses predsJson in a Try and sets preds to "" on failure; "" and "null" are no list too. Coverage (ontology-2): the edge-type parsing of the TraversalBFS string forms.
The weighted path procedure searches the graph that the query names. Without a name it searches each graph that has edges, and gives a row for each graph where it finds a path.

CALL ivg.shortestPath.weighted(from, to [, weightProp, maxCost, maxHops, direction, types]) YIELD path, totalCost: TraversalPaths.DijkstraJson per graph (DijkstraCost when only totalCost is yielded); a failed search or an answer that is not JSON raises (4.6.0 R155); missing from or to, or an options map, is refused (4.6.5). Coverage (ontology-2): ivg.shortestpath.weighted.
Given a list of candidate end nodes, the walk finds which of them it reaches and at what least depth. It walks one graph, out from the start node and back from each candidate.

VarLength.NamedEnds(pSrc, pTypes, pDir, pMinH, pMaxH, pGraph, .pCands, .pEnds) with pAll 0: a ball of (pMaxH + 1) \ 2 hops round pSrc, then each candidate's own ball walked backwards for the rest; a candidate is an end at its distance when that lies in pMinH..pMaxH. Graph.KG.Cypher.Exec calls it for a variable-length hop whose far node is fixed by an equality on at most 1,000 candidates (spec 253). It writes nothing. Coverage (ontology-2): VarLength.NamedEnds.

Each job takes its share of the level and writes the new nodes to a shared temporary area. The caller merges them in walk order and clears the area. There are at most eight jobs, and the count of processors is read once per process.

VarLength.LastLevelPart(pSrc, pTypes, pDir, pMaxH, pAll, pGraph, pShare, pPart, pParts, pShared) files ^IRIS.Temp.IVG.VL(pShare, "new"/"src"/"reads") and sets ^||IVG.VLWorker while it runs; LastLevel kills ^IRIS.Temp.IVG.VL(pShare). VarLength.CPUs keeps $System.Util.NumberOfCPUs() in ^||IVG.CPUs; the native executor's parallel checks call it too (Cypher/Exec.cls:291, 348, 381, 449). Coverage (ontology-2): VarLength.LastLevelPart, VarLength.CPUs.
The snapshot setup call writes an empty snapshot frame when none exists, with zero counts and the reserved labels. It leaves a snapshot that already has counts alone.

Traversal.InitNKGSkeleton -> TraversalBuild.InitNKGSkeleton: nothing when ^NKG("$meta","nodeCount") exists; else GraphIndex.InitStructuralLabels, nodeCount 0, edgeCount 0, version 0 when unset. The engine's incremental bulk-load session calls it outside a caller's transaction. Afterwards ^NKG("$meta") exists, so UseNKG answers 1 while the dictionary is empty. Coverage (ontology-2): Traversal.InitNKGSkeleton.
The snapshot count calls only read. They give its edge count, the next free node number, and the node count of the last rebuild. Another call says whether the snapshot holds any node.

Traversal.NKGEdgeCount ($meta edgeCount), NKGNodeCount ($meta nodeCount, the numbering high-water mark, never lowered), NKGLiveNodeCount ($meta liveNodes as the last rewrite counted them, else nodeCount), NKGPopulated (1 when ^NKG("$NI") has an entry; 4.6.0 R274), each delegating to TraversalBuild; 0 when unset. Callers: verify_sync, the index listing and status (admin.py:230, 488, 793-797), the bulk-load drift check (nodes_edges.py:507). Coverage (ontology-2): Traversal.NKGEdgeCount, Traversal.NKGNodeCount, Traversal.NKGLiveNodeCount, Traversal.NKGPopulated.
The adjacency index edge count adds up the edges of every graph. Several edges of one type between two nodes each count. It stops counting once it reaches its limit, 10,000 by default.

Traversal.KGEdgeCount(maxCount) -> TraversalBuild.KGEdgeCount: one per ^KG("out", g, s, p, o) leaf, a keyed triple's "#" count; the limit is checked between leaves, so a "#" count can carry it past (before 4.6.0 it counted sources). The status calls it with 10,000, the index listing with 1. Coverage (ontology-2): Traversal.KGEdgeCount.

In the USER namespace, when the optional library can be loaded, the build also asks it for two-hop counts over the snapshot. These merged counts are kept apart from the counts made for each graph. Elsewhere the call does nothing and answers zero.

NKGAccelTraversal.Build2HopExact: 0 outside USER; loads the BFS library (NKGAccelLoader.Load, else ArnoAccel's handle), calls kg_build_2hop_exact_stream, reads ^ArnoKG("2hs") parts or the inline {"data"} form, then replaces ^KG("deg2p_exact_merged", s, p) (spec 230 FR-011); a callout with no stream leaves the old counts. The exact-stats build calls it through NKGAccel, ignores the answer and puts the caller's namespace back (spec 236 R3). Coverage (ontology-2): NKGAccelTraversal.Build2HopExact, NKGAccel.Build2HopExact.

NKGAccelLoader.UseNKG ($Data(^NKG("$meta")) on each call, 4.6.0 R077; true after GraphIndex.DropNKG too, which leaves $meta("version")), IsLoaded (^||NKGAccel("dllid") and bfs_fn > 0), LoadedPath (^||NKGAccel("libPath"), 4.6.0 R132), LoadError (^||NKGAccel("loadError")). Coverage (ontology-2): NKGAccelLoader.UseNKG, NKGAccelLoader.IsLoaded, NKGAccelLoader.LoadedPath, NKGAccelLoader.LoadError and their NKGAccel delegators.

NKGAccelLoader.ResetCache and Unload both Kill ^||NKGAccel (dllid, libPath, bfs_fn, loadError, last_bfs_*); neither calls $ZF(-4,2). Coverage (ontology-2): NKGAccelLoader.ResetCache, NKGAccelLoader.Unload and their NKGAccel delegators.
The report of what can run says if a snapshot exists and if the Arno library answers. It lists the library's methods only when the library answers. Asking can load the library into the process.

NKGAccelLoader.Capabilities: JSON {version 0.1.0, nkg_accel, nkg_data (UseNKG), global_set, vec_index, rust_callout (the ArnoAccel availability check, which may load), algorithms [khop, random_walk, export_adjacency], rust_algorithms [ppr, pagerank, wcc, cdlp, bfs] only with the library, bfs, count_distinct_khop}; no ppr in algorithms since 4.6.0 R284. The store reads rust_callout and NKGAccel.IsLoaded to decide the library is absent. Coverage (ontology-2): NKGAccelLoader.Capabilities, NKGAccel.Capabilities.
The old call that asked the Arno library to build the snapshot is refused. It calls nothing and answers an error that names the server's own build.

NKGAccelLoader.BuildNKGRust answers {"error": "kg_build_nkg is deprecated (arno-callout 1.2.0) ... Graph.KG.Traversal.BuildNKG"}, a JSON text, not a throw. Coverage (ontology-2): NKGAccelLoader.BuildNKGRust, NKGAccel.BuildNKGRust.

A copy of the snapshot's edges for the Arno library is kept in a work area, with the snapshot version it was made from. A snapshot build clears it, and the warm call makes it again only when the version has moved.

NKGAccelLoader.InvalidateAdjCache kills ^ArnoKG("KG","nkg_adj_ver") and ("KG","nkg_adj"); WarmAdjCache runs CacheNKGAdj (ExportAdjacency into ^ArnoKG("KG","nkg_adj", n) in 32,000-character parts, marked with ^NKG("$meta","version")) and answers the part count. BuildNKG calls InvalidateAdjCache before and after its rewrite. No product code reads ^ArnoKG("KG","nkg_adj"). Coverage (ontology-2): NKGAccelLoader.InvalidateAdjCache, NKGAccelLoader.WarmAdjCache and their NKGAccel delegators.

The library's status calls change nothing. They give the file this process loaded, whether the file to load exists, the path last recorded, and the loaded build's version name. None of them loads the library.

ArnoAccel.LoadedPath (^||ArnoAccel("path")), LibExists (%File.Exists of LibPath(pPath)), GetLibPath (^ArnoAccel("lib_path") as recorded, not checked by TrustedPath), LibraryVersion (the version entry through this process's handle, "" without one; routing never reads it). engine.status() reads LoadedPath and LibExists (ALG-B13.10), and LibraryVersion once the library is available. Coverage (ontology-2): ArnoAccel.LoadedPath, ArnoAccel.LibExists, ArnoAccel.GetLibPath, ArnoAccel.LibraryVersion.
The check of whether the library can run says no at once when no load has saved a library path. Else it asks this process's handle for the version. When that fails, it loads the library again.

ArnoAccel.IsAvailable: no ^ArnoAccel("lib_path") gives 0; Handle() is this process's id only for the recorded path; a failed version call runs Load(), which resolves LibPath (a trusted recorded path, else the default; 4.6.0 R311) and records ^ArnoAccel("lib_path") on success. Called by the store's reload, NKGAccelLoader.Capabilities, NKGAccelTraversal.Build2HopExact and TraversalBuild.ArnoCapabilities. Coverage (ontology-2): ArnoAccel.IsAvailable.

Some calls of the library class do not use the Arno library at all. These are PageRank, its form with start nodes, components, label spreading and subgraph. Each passes the call to the algorithm owner and gives its answer.

ArnoAccel.PageRankGlobalJson -> PageRank.PageRankGlobalJson, PPRJson -> PageRank.RunJson, WCCJson -> Algorithms.WCCJson, CDLPJson -> Algorithms.CDLPJson, SubgraphJson -> Subgraph.SubgraphJson (the library's readers walked ^KG unreliably); the native readers are the *NativeJson methods (ALG-D3). Coverage (ontology-2): ArnoAccel.PPRJson, ArnoAccel.WCCJson, ArnoAccel.CDLPJson.
The sample helpers read a copy of the default graph's nodes and edges kept in a work area. The copy is made again whenever the token has moved.

ArnoAccel.BuildGraphJson: {"nodes": the default graph's ^KG out and in keys, "edges": [{src, dst, type}]} (GraphKey.ForIndex(""), one per triple; a node with no edge is not in it); CacheGraphJson (private) keeps it in ^ArnoKG("KG","graph_json") with ^KG("__version") and is reached only in USER (KhopSampleJson, RandomWalkJson, NeighborAggJson; ALG-B13.11). The class doc's ^||ArnoKG.JSON is not where it is kept. Coverage (ontology-2): ArnoAccel.BuildGraphJson.
For label spreading, the gate first needs every repeat to give the same labels as the first. Its groups must then share enough node pairs with the algorithm owner's groups.

_arno_gate.cdlp_equivalent(repeats, owner, threshold): repeats_identical (canonical rows; order is not identity), then partition_similarity (Jaccard over the node pairs each partition puts together; 1.0 when neither has any) at or above threshold; scripts/arno_reader_gate.py passes CDLP_THRESHOLD 0.8. Coverage (ontology-2): cdlp_equivalent, repeats_identical, partition_similarity.
One server call raises the token and the snapshot's version count by one each. An erase and a restore both use it, so every cached answer then counts as out of date.

ArnoAccel.BumpVersion: $Increment(^KG("__version")) and $Increment(^NKG("$meta","version")), atomic and not undone by a rollback (ALG-P2). Eraser.InvalidateDerived and the restore's _raise_kg_version call it; the snapshot version also ages the library's copy of the snapshot (ALG-B13.94). Coverage (ontology-2): ArnoAccel.BumpVersion.
Setup asked for over the web deploys no classes unless the request asks for them. The schema init command never asks.

AdminSchemaRequest.auto_deploy_objectscript defaults to False (cypher_api.py:571-575), while initialize_schema() defaults to True; ivg schema init posts only embedding_dimension and rewidth. docs/ADMIN_API.md:225-234 names the flag and sends it as true in its example, but gives no default. docs/ADMIN_GUIDE.md:214-217: a namespace set up without the class deploy has the tables and none of the behaviour; the schema record is saved all the same (INS-Q1.15, HD-0102). Route semantics: module API (API-B8.10); the command: module OPS (OPS-B1.8). Coverage (ontology-2): POST /admin/schema/init, ivg schema init.
Reading the schema record gives the saved schema name. A missing or empty record reads as none.

read_record(native): one get of ^IVG.Deploy("schema"); None when it is undefined or "". Read by check_first_access and refuse_other_record (schema_name.py:189, 226), setup (_engine/schema.py:2222), status (_engine/admin.py:423) and the sample API's database_problem (api/main.py:56). Coverage (ontology-2): schema_name.read_record.
Setup reads the rights on all the objects it looks at in one query. Each right says how it is held: on the object, through its schema, as owner, or as a full-rights user.

grants_by_object(conn, sql_names): one SELECT over "%Library".SQLAllPrivileges, names matched without regard to case; via is Direct, Schema Privilege, Owner Privilege or SuperUser; GRANTED_BY is read as %INTERNAL and parsed by _grantors. Used by present_legacy_objects, grant_read_path and revoke_legacy_arno (legacy.py:165, 401, 550, 577). Before 4.6.0 fixes74 it was one Native API result set per object, hours over a slow link. Coverage (ontology-2): grants_by_object.
Setup looks for library wrappers in every schema. It finds each one by its exact name, never by a pattern.

arno_copies(conn): INFORMATION_SCHEMA.ROUTINES rows whose name starts ivg_arno_, kept only when the upper-case name is one of ARNO_WRAPPERS (the legacy manifest's SQLUser ivg_arno_* names), as schema, name and body. 4.5.x made them in the instance's default SQL schema, so a copy may be in any schema. Setup and its preview read it only with a native handle (_engine/schema.py:2257, 2294); replace_arno_wrappers and revoke_legacy_arno act on it (INS-B6.8, INS-B6.9). Coverage (ontology-2): arno_copies.
Setup adds the graph column to an edge table that lacks it. It also adds two edge indexes that start with the graph.

add_graph_id_column: ALTER TABLE rdf_edges ADD COLUMN graph_id VARCHAR(256) %EXACT NULL. add_graph_id_index: idx_edges_graph_id (graph_id). add_graph_oid_index: idx_edges_graph_oid (graph_id, o_id), 4.5.2, for a bare-node retire and fk_edges_dest. An answer that it is already there counts as done; any other error answers False with no log line, and setup does not read ensure_indexes' answer (_engine/schema.py:2514). Coverage (ontology-2): add_graph_id_column, add_graph_id_index, add_graph_oid_index.
Setup adds a number column to the edge table and puts it in the unique key. Old rows get zero. The old key is dropped only once the new one is in place.

ensure_ekey: five steps, each skipped when the catalog shows it done, so a run cut short resumes: add ekey INTEGER DEFAULT 0, fill 0, NOT NULL, add u_spo_graph_ekey UNIQUE (s, p, o_id, graph_id, ekey), drop u_spo_graph. A failure logs a WARNING and answers status failed with the steps done; setup does not read it (_engine/schema.py:2514). Unit tests on a fake cursor. Coverage (ontology-2): ensure_ekey.
Before the number goes in the key, setup moves the edge table to a unique key that holds the graph.

update_spo_unique_constraint: drops u_spo and uspo (errors ignored) and adds u_spo_graph UNIQUE (s, p, o_id, graph_id); True when added or already there. _spo_constraint_status skips it once ekey is NOT NULL and u_spo_graph_ekey exists (_at_234), so it never puts the narrower key back. Coverage (ontology-2): update_spo_unique_constraint.
Setup gives the property table a column with the first part of each value, and an index on key and that column. It fills old rows in batches and makes the index last.

ensure_props_value_key: val_key VARCHAR(128) %EXACT, computed as the first 128 characters of val (COMPUTEONCHANGE); backfill UPDATE ... SET val = val, VALUE_KEY_BATCH = 200000 rows a statement; a backfill that stops moving leaves the index uncreated; an idx_props_key_valkey over (key, val) is dropped and made again on (key, val_key). Each step is skipped when the catalog shows it done. A failure is a WARNING log only. Unit tests on fakes. Coverage (ontology-2): ensure_props_value_key.
Setup makes the value column of the property table long and exact in case. It alters it only when IRIS shows it is not so already.

upgrade_val_column: reads %Dictionary.PropertyDefinition of Graph.KG.rdfprops val; runs ALTER TABLE rdf_props ALTER COLUMN val VARCHAR(64000) COLLATE %EXACT unless it shows MAXLEN 64000 and EXACT collation (or cannot be read). A WARNING first says IRIS rebuilds the indexes on val. False on a failed ALTER. Coverage (ontology-2): upgrade_val_column.
Setup adds the graph column to the node table. Each time, it then moves any old graph property of a node into that column and deletes the property.

add_graph_id_to_nodes(recreate_pk=False), run by ensure_indexes on every setup: ALTER TABLE nodes ADD COLUMN graph_id VARCHAR(256) %EXACT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''; UPDATE nodes SET graph_id from the rdf_props row with key '__graph' of the same node id (no graph match); DELETE every rdf_props row with key '__graph'; then a commit on the cursor's connection. A failed step is a WARNING log. The rebuild of nodes with a compound key runs only with recreate_pk=True, which nothing in the product passes, though CHANGELOG.md:5253-5255 says setup recreates it. create_node does not refuse a property named __graph (nodes_edges.py:1055-1058). Coverage (ontology-2): add_graph_id_to_nodes.
One call returns the index text as a single script. Nothing in the product runs it, and setup makes its indexes one at a time instead.

GraphSchema.get_indexes_sql(): CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS for eleven indexes, plus idx_props_val_ifind and idx_edges_confidence; no caller at the pin outside tests. ensure_indexes runs its own list, which adds idx_docs_graph, idx_docs_text_ifind and the drop of idx_props_key_val. Coverage (ontology-2): get_indexes_sql.
The node re-key of the upgrade has a fixed order. It drops the keys that hold the old node key, keys nodes by graph, gives labels and properties their graph, and then puts the keys back.

GraphSchema.get_graph_scope_migration_sql(legacy_node_keys), spec 227 contracts/sql-schema.md section 4: the list is returned, not run; graph_scoped_embeddings._rekey_children runs it (module VEC, VEC-X10.10 states its refusal). Every statement is safe to repeat. Coverage (ontology-2): get_graph_scope_migration_sql.
The re-key refuses an old key name that is not plain. It hands back no statements then.
ValueError "not a constraint name this migration can drop" for a legacy_node_keys name outside [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*; uq_nodes_nodeid is skipped, as the list always drops it.

Before a statement runs, its schema and vector width are filled in. The width is written as a whole number, so it cannot carry other text.

bind(name, schema, dimension, dtype, table): STATEMENTS[name] with {schema}, {suffix} (_ivg400), {dtype} upper case, {dim} as int(dimension) or empty, and {table}; an unknown name raises KeyError. bind_all binds each name in order. Used by migrations/docs_and_edge_vectors.py (module VEC's step). Spec 240 still says not adopted (F-0104). Coverage (ontology-2): bind, bind_all.

CypherFn_IVGREGEXMATCH, _IVGJSONARRAYLENGTH, _IVGJSONVALUE, _IVGJSONKEYS, _IVGLISTREVERSE, _IVGSTRSPLIT, _IVGNEWID, _IVGRAND, _IVGLISTHEAD, _IVGLISTLAST, _IVGLISTTAIL, _IVGLISTGET, _IVGTYPEERROR, _IVGMAPGET, _IVGJSONSET, _IVGJSONREMOVE, _IVGRANGE: each Quit ##class(Graph.KG.CypherFn).IVG<name>(args), no check before. Setup's deploy compiles the class (INS-B4.13); what each answers is module CYP's. Coverage (ontology-2): the sixteen CypherFnIVG* methods at SqlProcs.cls:22-100.
The forwarder class gives the three transaction calls of a write their SQL names: begin, end and undo. Each passes its level on and returns the answer.

The Python ledger client pages through it (module LED). Coverage (ontology-2): LedgerRecords, LedgerRecordsFetch, LedgerRecordsClose.

sql/operators.sql: kg_TXT, kg_GRAPH_PATH, kg_RERANK, kg_PPR (lines 32, 86, 106, 134; CYP-T15.3 states the file); sql/operators_fixed.sql: kg_TXT, kg_GRAPH_PATH, kg_RERANK (lines 32, 73, 96), which scripts/deploy_production.py runs; sql/graph_path_globals.sql: kg_GRAPH_PATH, kg_SHORTEST_PATH, kg_NODE_STATS (lines 5, 143, 283), Python bodies that read ^KG; sql/graph_walk_tvf.sql: Graph_Neighborhood_Expansion (line 72), a stub that returns one fixed row. idx_edges_s_p, idx_edges_p_oid, idx_edges_s, idx_edges_oid on rdf_edges; HNSW_NodeEmb on kg_NodeEmbeddings(emb) (768 wide, cosine); a word index on docs(text) (line 53), TYPE BITMAP with word parameters. Graph_KG.fhir_bridges with idx_bridges_code_type, idx_bridges_kg_node and idx_bridges_type; Graph_KG.rdf_reifications with idx_reif_edge. On success verify_deployment looks for Graph_Walk, Graph_Neighborhood_Expansion and Vector_Graph_Search and calls Graph_Walk once. Exit 1 on failure. Not shipped (pyproject.toml:181-183).
