A schema check call reads one row from each of seven tables and says which ones answered. The node table is not one of them.

GraphSchema.validate_schema(cursor): SELECT TOP 1 * FROM rdf_labels, rdf_props, rdf_edges, kg_NodeEmbeddings, kg_NodeEmbeddings_optimized, kg_EdgeEmbeddings and docs, named in Graph_KG; any error is False. No caller in the package; examples/domains/biomedical_legacy/biomedical_schema.py:246 and tests call it. Coverage (ontology-2): validate_schema.
To find the class that holds a table, the product asks IRIS. If IRIS names none, the product guesses the name from the table name.

GraphSchema.resolve_table_class reads %Dictionary.CompiledClass by SqlSchemaName and SqlTableName (names sanitized and put in the text); a bad name is a WARNING and None, a failed read a DEBUG log or an entry in errors. GraphSchema.derive_class_name: schema underscores become dots and table underscores go (Graph_KG.kg_NodeEmbeddings gives Graph.KG.kgNodeEmbeddings). get_embedding_dimension and _declared_vector_dtype use the guess when the lookup gives None; hnsw_indexes uses the lookup only. Coverage (ontology-2): resolve_table_class, derive_class_name.
A write that first looks for a row tells IRIS not to use the key or label index. So a load into a new namespace does not slow down as it grows.

guard_from(table): FROM %IGNOREINDEX <t>.idx_props_key, <t>.idx_props_key_valkey on rdf_props and %IGNOREINDEX <t>.idx_labels_label on rdf_labels; ValueError for any other table. Used by create_node, store_node (nodes_edges.py:2484-2491) and translator._hint_row_guards; the bulk SQL templates spell the same FROM. On statistics taken near empty the plan read the key-first index, every row with that key (4.7.0). Unit test. Coverage (ontology-2): guard_from.
A two-hop count refuses an empty or blank node id before it asks IRIS.

KHop2Input, run first by khop2_count_fast and khop2_count_exact, before Graph.KG.Traversal is called; the ValueError reaches the caller as a pydantic ValidationError. It checks node_id only, not the predicate. Unit test. Coverage (ontology-2): KHop2Input, KHop2Input.must_be_nonempty.
The check for one timed edge refuses an empty or blank source, type or target. It also refuses a time or a weight below zero.

TemporalEdgeInput: timestamp ge=0, weight ge=0.0 (default 1.0), source, predicate and target non-blank. create_edge_temporal runs it only when a timestamp is given; delete_edge_temporal always runs it; the batch path does not (F-0513; module 05 states the paths in TMP-X1.13 and TMP-X4.7). Unit tests. Coverage (ontology-2): TemporalEdgeInput, TemporalEdgeInput.source_nonempty, TemporalEdgeInput.predicate_nonempty, TemporalEdgeInput.target_nonempty.
The millisecond index can report one source's bucket count in one time bucket of a graph. It only reads.

Graph.KG.TemporalIndexMS.GetBucketCount(graphId, bucket, node) answers +$Get(^KG("bucket", GraphKey.ForIndex(graphId), bucket, node), 0): the source's live temporal edges of every type in that bucket, raised by each write and lowered by each delete. The caller passes the bucket number. The store is shared, so writes in seconds count too (TMP-T1.22). Public class method with no product caller; its comment says tests use it. Coverage (ontology-2): TemporalIndexMS.GetBucketCount.
Looking up a known hash gives back the sorted form stored under it.

IRISGraphEngine.resolve_label_set(hash_hex) calls the store, which calls Graph.KG.TemporalIndex.ResolveLabelSet: $Get(^KG("labelset", hash), ""). A null answer becomes "". It reads no graph: label sets are shared by the namespace. Coverage (ontology-2): resolve_label_set.
Its walk, group, subgraph, neighbour, PageRank and rerank calls pass each input on as given. They add nothing and drop nothing.

IRISGraphOperators.kg_GRAPH_WALK, kg_GRAPH_WALK_TVF, kg_WCC, kg_CDLP, kg_SUBGRAPH, kg_NEIGHBORS, kg_MENTIONS, kg_PPR and kg_RERANK call the IRISGraphEngine method of the same name with the same arguments and the same defaults; kg_NEIGHBORHOOD_EXPANSION passes *args and **kwargs through, graph= too. None of the others takes a graph, and neither do their engine methods. The engine is the one the class built over its connection. What the targets do is modules 06 and 10's. Coverage (ontology-2): IRISGraphOperators.kg_GRAPH_WALK, IRISGraphOperators.kg_GRAPH_WALK_TVF, IRISGraphOperators.kg_NEIGHBORHOOD_EXPANSION, IRISGraphOperators.kg_WCC, IRISGraphOperators.kg_CDLP, IRISGraphOperators.kg_SUBGRAPH, IRISGraphOperators.kg_NEIGHBORS, IRISGraphOperators.kg_MENTIONS, IRISGraphOperators.kg_PPR, IRISGraphOperators.kg_RERANK.
The guided subgraph call also takes two older input names. When given, each one wins over the input it stands for.

IRISGraphOperators.kg_PPR_GUIDED_SUBGRAPH: top_k, when not None, replaces ppr_top_k, and max_hops replaces k_hops; damping, max_iterations, edge_types and max_nodes pass unchanged, with the engine's defaults, to IRISGraphEngine.kg_PPR_GUIDED_SUBGRAPH. Coverage (ontology-2): IRISGraphOperators.kg_PPR_GUIDED_SUBGRAPH.
In read-only mode, a show command, or the label query that the Neo4j Browser sends, is judged by its words, since the parser cannot read it. It counts as a write only if it holds a write word.

answered_without_parsing(upper) is true when the upper-cased, stripped statement starts with SHOW, or holds both CALL DB.LABELS() YIELD and UNION: the texts execute_cypher answers before the parser (CYP-D16). Such a statement is judged by _names_a_write_clause: a CREATE, MERGE, DELETE, DETACH, SET, REMOVE or FOREACH token makes it a write, and a text that does not lex counts as one. An EXPLAIN prefix is cut off first. Coverage (ontology-2): answered_without_parsing.
A caller can ask for the schema name the translator uses when it has no engine. It is empty until a caller sets one.

get_schema_prefix() returns the module value _schema_prefix that set_schema_prefix sets ("" at import); iris_vector_graph.cypher exports both. An empty value means Graph_KG (_current_prefix). A translation for an engine uses that engine's schema_prefix and reads this only when the engine has none (engine.py:339-342). TextSearchEngine takes it as its default schema when none is passed. Coverage (ontology-2): get_schema_prefix.
A link mapping lets an edge between two mapped labels be read from a key column or a join table. It is kept once for the namespace, with no graph.

IRISGraphEngine.map_sql_relationship(source_label, predicate, target_label, target_fk or via_table with via_source and via_target) upserts one relationship_mappings row, which has no graph column, in one write_txn, and clears the engine's mapping cache. Its refusals are module 15's INT-M1.6. _trp_mapped_relation joins the target table on target_fk, or through via_table, for a one-type edge between two mapped labels, whatever graph the query names (see CYP-Q4.17). The names are checked by sanitize_identifier when a query is translated, not when they are stored. Such edges are not in the adjacency index (INT-M1.1). Coverage (ontology-2): map_sql_relationship.
Thirteen of the helper functions in IRIS are called by no translation. Plain SQL, or a dotted function name in a query, can still call them.

At the pin the translator's _fn sites name four Graph.KG.CypherFn helpers: IVGJSONSET, IVGJSONREMOVE, IVGTYPEERROR and IVGRANGE. IVGREGEXMATCH, IVGJSONARRAYLENGTH, IVGJSONVALUE, IVGJSONKEYS, IVGLISTREVERSE, IVGSTRSPLIT, IVGNEWID, IVGRAND, IVGLISTHEAD, IVGLISTLAST, IVGLISTTAIL, IVGLISTGET and IVGMAPGET are called by no translator code and no ObjectScript class. Cypher's =~, list index, size, keys, reverse, tail, split, randomUUID and rand use the schema.py functions REGEX_MATCH, JSON_ARRAYGET, JSON_ARRAYLENGTH, JSON_KEYS, CY_REVERSE, LIST_TAIL, STR_SPLIT, NEWID and RAND instead. Each helper stays projected as <IVG Schema>.CypherFn_IVG<Name> by Graph.KG.SqlProcs, so SQL or a dotted name in Cypher (CYP-T11.2) reaches it. Coverage (ontology-2): none by itself; CYP-T11.91 to CYP-T11.103 state each helper.

The list helper functions answer a JSON list's first item, its last item, all but the first, or all items in reverse. With no list, an empty one, or text that is not JSON, the first two answer null. The other two answer an empty list.

Graph.KG.CypherFn.IVGLISTHEAD and IVGLISTLAST answer "" (SQL NULL), IVGLISTTAIL and IVGLISTREVERSE "[]", for "", "null", [] or text %FromJSON cannot read. Head and last answer %Get's value with no %ToJSON, so a nested list or map item does not come back as JSON (JSON_ARRAYGET of schema.py does that). Integration tests (live IRIS). Coverage (ontology-2): CypherFn.IVGLISTHEAD, CypherFn.IVGLISTLAST, CypherFn.IVGLISTTAIL, CypherFn.IVGLISTREVERSE.
The list length helper function counts the items of a JSON list. It answers 0 for no list or for text that is not JSON.
Graph.KG.CypherFn.IVGJSONARRAYLENGTH: %Size() of the parsed JSON; 0 for "", "null" or unreadable text. Integration tests (live IRIS). Coverage (ontology-2): CypherFn.IVGJSONARRAYLENGTH.
The JSON value helper function takes a path of one step: a key after a dollar sign and a dot, or an item number in brackets for a list. Any other path, or a missing value, answers null.

Graph.KG.CypherFn.IVGJSONVALUE(json, path): $.<rest> answers %Get(<rest>), the whole rest as one key, so $.a.b reads a key named a.b, not a nested value; $[N] answers item N only when the JSON is a list. "", "null" or unreadable JSON answer "" (NULL). A nested value does not come back as JSON. Cypher's own reads use JSON_VALUE of schema.py. Integration tests (live IRIS). Coverage (ontology-2): CypherFn.IVGJSONVALUE.
The key helper functions read a JSON map. One answers its keys as a JSON list, and one answers the value of one key. With no map, they answer an empty list and null.

Graph.KG.CypherFn.IVGJSONKEYS answers the keys in the object's order, "[]" for "", "null" or unreadable JSON. Graph.KG.CypherFn.IVGMAPGET(json, key) answers %Get(key): "" (NULL) for a missing key, no map or unreadable JSON; SQL's '' as the key reads as the empty key (4.6.0 R269). Integration and unit tests. Coverage (ontology-2): CypherFn.IVGJSONKEYS, CypherFn.IVGMAPGET.
The split helper function cuts a text at each delimiter into a JSON list. An empty delimiter gives one item per character. A null text gives an empty list, not a null.

Graph.KG.CypherFn.IVGSTRSPLIT(s, delim): $Piece by delim; SQL's '' as delim gives the characters (4.6.0 R269); a null text answers "[]", and a null delimiter gives $Length(s, "") = 0 pieces, so "[]" too. Cypher's split() uses STR_SPLIT of schema.py, which answers NULL for a null input. Coverage (ontology-2): CypherFn.IVGSTRSPLIT.
The new id helper function answers a new random unique id on each call. The random helper function answers a fraction from 0 up to 1, never 1, in steps of one millionth.

Graph.KG.CypherFn.IVGNEWID: $SYSTEM.Util.CreateGUID(). Graph.KG.CypherFn.IVGRAND: $Random(1000000) / 1000000. Cypher's randomUUID() and rand() use NEWID and RAND of schema.py, the same formulas (translator.py:26920-26924). Integration test (live IRIS). Coverage (ontology-2): CypherFn.IVGNEWID, CypherFn.IVGRAND.
The type error helper function always fails, with the message it is given. A translation calls it where a value has the wrong type for what the query does with it.

Graph.KG.CypherFn.IVGTYPEERROR(msg) throws %Exception.General("TypeError", 5001, , msg). _row_error_sql makes the message depend on the row's values, since IRIS runs a call with constant arguments once when the query opens (4.6.0 R297). Used for a list index or a map key of the wrong type, among others. Integration test (live IRIS). Coverage (ontology-2): CypherFn.IVGTYPEERROR.
The set helper function writes one key into a JSON map and answers the new map. With no map, it starts an empty one.

Graph.KG.CypherFn.IVGJSONSET(json, key, val, typ): a new %DynamicObject for "", "null" or a non-object; answers %ToJSON(). A Cypher SET of an edge property writes the edge's qualifiers with it. Integration tests (live IRIS). Coverage (ontology-2): CypherFn.IVGJSONSET.
The set helper function stores the value as text, a number, or a list or map, as the translation asks. With no type given, text that reads as a number is stored as a number.

typ "string": %Set(key, val, "string"); "json": parsed as a list or map (4.6.0 R305); "number", or no typ and $IsValidNum text: +val; else the text. The translator passes "string", "number" or "json" for a literal or a parameter (_json_set_type, _set_value_is_json), and no type for an expression, whose numeric text then becomes a number. SQL's '' as the value stays $Char(0), stored as \u0000, so it reads back as ''. Unit test (source). Coverage (ontology-2): CypherFn.IVGJSONSET.
The remove helper function takes one key out of a JSON map and answers the rest. With no map, it answers an empty map.

Graph.KG.CypherFn.IVGJSONREMOVE(json, key): "{}" for "", $Char(0) or "null"; else %Remove(key), and a missing key leaves the map as it is. SET r.k = null and REMOVE r.k on an edge use it. Integration and unit tests. Coverage (ontology-2): CypherFn.IVGJSONREMOVE.
When the map, or a list or map value, is not valid JSON, the set and remove helper functions answer the map as it was. No error is raised, so the write changes nothing.

Catch { Return json } in Graph.KG.CypherFn.IVGJSONSET and IVGJSONREMOVE: a SET or REMOVE of a property of an edge whose qualifiers text is not JSON leaves that text, and the UPDATE counts the row as written. Coverage (ontology-2): CypherFn.IVGJSONSET, CypherFn.IVGJSONREMOVE.
The range helper function lists the numbers from a start up to an end, by a step. The end is in the list when a step lands on it. A step of 0 gives an empty list, not an error.

Graph.KG.CypherFn.IVGRANGE(start, end, step), step 1 by default: a For loop up to end for a positive step, a While i >= end for a negative one, so a step that points away from the end gives []. The translator also uses it to number the rows of a long UNWIND (translator.py:9024-9030). Integration tests (live IRIS). Coverage (ontology-2): CypherFn.IVGRANGE.
A range with a step known only at run time uses the range helper function. So a step of 0 there gives an empty list, though a step of 0 written in the query is refused.

_expr_fn_range raises ValueError NumberOutOfRange for a literal step of 0; a step read from the row (a variable, or a parameter the translator does not inline) is not known, so range() becomes CypherFn_IVGRANGE(start, end, step), which answers [] for 0. The TCK (List11 [4]) expects an ArgumentError for a step of 0 and tests it only with literals. Coverage (ontology-2): CypherFn.IVGRANGE.
A refused insert counts as a row already there when its error text names a unique key.

is_duplicate: true when the text holds unique (any case) or -119. Used by _skip_duplicate (the SQL adapter's guarded inserts) and the inference writer. After a BUILD INDEX IRIS can answer a repeat as <LIST ERROR>, which this test misses, so that repeat is raised (F-C1110). Coverage (ontology-2): is_duplicate.
The engine's node and edge counts cover one graph. With no graph named, they count the default graph.

count_nodes(label, graph) counts that label's rows in the graph, or its node rows; node_count and edge_count go through _count_in_graph, where a NULL graph_id is the default graph. Each runs the name check first (GID-T3.9), and a failed query raises. Each parallel edge counts. engine.status() counts every graph together (API-T8.9). Coverage (ontology-2): count_nodes, node_count, edge_count.
The engine's lookups by label, by property or by id pattern read every graph together. A caller cannot pick one graph, and an id held in two graphs can come back twice.

get_node_ids_by_label, get_node_ids_by_property, get_property_pairs, get_property_values, property_value_exists, get_property_pairs_like, get_json_field_values, get_node_ids_like (a SQL LIKE pattern over node ids) and count_subjects_with_property: one-table reads of rdf_labels, rdf_props or nodes with no graph_id filter. get_nodes_by_label then reads the default graph's copy of each id. Whether a read that names no graph should read the default graph is open (GID-Q6.11, HD-0201). Coverage (ontology-2): get_node_ids_by_label, get_node_ids_by_property, get_property_pairs, get_property_values, property_value_exists, get_property_pairs_like, get_json_field_values, get_node_ids_like, count_subjects_with_property.
With a limit, a lookup by property answers the first rows it meets, in no set order.

get_node_ids_by_property and get_property_pairs_like build SELECT TOP n with no ORDER BY; a limit of 0 or less means no limit. Coverage (ontology-2): get_node_ids_by_property, get_property_pairs_like.
Erasing all graphs empties every graph, and the shared stores made from their content. The ledger's records stay, and so do the vectors set aside for want of a graph.

erase_all: the strict check first (WRT-X1.2), then Graph.KG.Eraser.EraseAll in one transaction: the route tables, the embedding registry, labels, properties, docs, the legacy vector tables, edges, nodes, the adjacency (Adjacency.RemoveAll), the temporal stores, the ^KG label, prop, labelset and two-hop subtrees, ^NKG and the derived stores, ^ArnoKG, graph modes, opt-out lists, the result cache and the ledger's stmt and tuple indexes. ^IVG.Ledger(rec) and Graph_KG.embedding_quarantine stay. Claimed route tables are dropped after the commit. It answers the count of node and edge rows removed, then clears the engine's route memory and graph modes. Module ERS owns the eraser. Coverage (ontology-2): erase_all.
Asking which ids are nodes checks every graph. A lookup IRIS refuses raises, so a refused id never reads as missing.
nodes_exist: ids in batches of 200 in one IN list; a refused batch is asked again one id at a time, and a refused id raises RuntimeError (4.6.0 R276). Coverage (ontology-2): nodes_exist.
A node's name is read from the default graph: its name property, else its label property, else its title.
get_node_name over get_node_properties (get_node of the default graph); None when the node or all three are missing, and an empty value counts as missing. Coverage (ontology-2): get_node_name.
A field lookup takes one text field out of each JSON value under a key, on the server. It finds the field only when it is written in one fixed way.

get_json_field_values: $PIECE after the text "field": " (one space after the colon) up to the next double quote, over the rows whose val is LIKE %field%; a number, a list, other spacing or an escaped quote gives nothing or a cut value, and empty results are dropped. The field name is pasted into the SQL text and into the LIKE pattern as given. Coverage (ontology-2): get_json_field_values.
An engine can be made on a connection that the wrapper package opens. With no address, that works only inside IRIS. Such an engine never reconnects on its own.

IRISGraphEngine.from_wrapper: iris-embedded-python-wrapper's dbapi.connect over TCP when hostname is given; else an embedded connection when the runtime state is embedded, else RuntimeError; ImportError when the wrapper is missing. Unlike from_connect it keeps no connection parameters. Coverage (ontology-2): from_wrapper.
The property lookups give a number back as a number. A list, a map, true or false comes back as the text it is stored as.

get_property_pairs, get_property_values and get_property_pairs_like read val through CY_TYPED and decode_typed_text: a value marked as a $DOUBLE, an integer or a decimal comes back as a float or an int. Unlike get_node (WRT-B5.4, WRT-B5.5) they decode no list or map text and no stored true or false. get_property_values drops empty values. Coverage (ontology-2): get_property_pairs, get_property_values, get_property_pairs_like, decode_typed_text.
A test that stored text equals a number accepts each text the number may be stored as, such as .95 and 0.95.

number_spellings: the ObjectScript canonical form (.95), str(v), json.dumps(v) and the plain decimal (4.6.0 R121, R307). The Cypher translator's number tests and the bound id reader use it. Coverage (ontology-2): number_spellings.
A query column known to hold a list, a map or a path is read from its JSON text. Text there that is not JSON stays text, with a warning.

decode_json_value over SQLQuery.json_value_columns (4.6.0 R311), in _decode_json_value_columns; a value already decoded and null pass through, and NaN reads as a float. Coverage (ontology-2): decode_json_value.
When IRIS builds the label index again, its start and end steps do nothing. Each label row goes in as one insert.

Graph.KG.LabelIndex.SortBeginIndex and SortEndIndex answer $$$OK; a build runs PurgeIndex, then InsertIndex (Adjacency.PutLabel) for each row. Coverage (ontology-2): LabelIndex.SortBeginIndex, LabelIndex.SortEndIndex.
When the caller has a transaction open, the server loader runs in the caller's own IRIS process. Its rows then join that transaction.

WriteTxn.native: iris.createIRIS on the connection itself (InProcessHost for an embedded connection), never the engine's own Native API connection; bulk_create_nodes and bulk_ingest_edges use it when txn.joined, and so does the ledger client. With no caller transaction they use the engine's _iris_obj (WRT-B3.19, F-0305). Coverage (ontology-2): WriteTxn.native.
The bulk loader can also run as a command. It loads a saved networkx graph from a file into one graph.

bulk_loader.main (python -m iris_vector_graph.bulk_loader PICKLE): reads the file with pickle.load, which runs code the file holds, so only a trusted file is safe; opens its own DB-API connection (defaults localhost:1972/USER, user and password test); --graph (default the default graph), --noindex on by default, --no-globals, --batch-size, --label-attr; then BulkLoader.load_networkx and a printed summary. Coverage (ontology-2): bulk_loader.main.
The temporal mark is a qualifier named temporal that holds true, or 1 as a number or as text. So an edge row another writer made with it is taken for a temporal one, and can be deleted.

Adjacency.IsTemporalMarked: %FromJSON of the qualifiers, then %Get(temporal) = 1, which JSON true, 1 and the string 1 all pass. RetractTemporalRow and TemporalPolicy.DropRows delete by it. The ledger stores qualifier values as strings, so a recorded relationship with temporal=1 is deleted as a temporal edge's row while its statement stays live (F-C0450). Coverage (ontology-2): IsTemporalMarked.
When IRIS builds the row hook's index again, the start and end steps of the build do nothing. Each row goes in as one insert.

Graph.KG.AdjIndex.SortBeginIndex and SortEndIndex answer $$$OK; %BuildIndices runs PurgeIndex, then InsertIndex (Adjacency.RowPut) for every row (ADJ-B2.9, ADJ-B8.2). Coverage (ontology-2): AdjIndex.SortBeginIndex, AdjIndex.SortEndIndex.
A bulk load can first set up an empty interned snapshot. Each edge it then adds is numbered there at once.

TraversalBuild.InitNKGSkeleton (through Graph.KG.Traversal): when ^NKG has no nodeCount, it reserves the fixed labels and sets nodeCount and edgeCount to 0; one that exists is left alone. bulk_load_session(incremental=True) calls it outside a caller transaction, and Adjacency.Put interns from then on (ADJ-T3.1.2). Coverage (ontology-2): InitNKGSkeleton.
Each edge type gets a number in the interned snapshot too, and keeps it for good. The first three numbers are kept for fixed names.

GraphIndex.InternLabel: ^NKG($LI, label) read with no lock, else taken under a lock on that name as the next $meta labelCount; GraphIndex.InitStructuralLabels reserves out, in and deg as 0, 1 and 2, once. Callers: Adjacency.Put and TraversalBuild.WalkSource. Coverage (ontology-2): InternLabel, InitStructuralLabels.
A lookup of a node's or an edge type's number in the interned snapshot never makes one. It answers empty when there is none.
GraphIndex.GetNodeIdx and GraphIndex.GetLabelIdx; their caller is NKGAccelTraversal.CountDistinctKHop. Coverage (ontology-2): GetNodeIdx, GetLabelIdx.
Adding an edge to the interned snapshot also adds its target to a small sketch, kept per source and edge type. The sketches are used to guess how many nodes a walk reaches.

GraphIndex.UpdateStructuralHLL: a 256-register HyperLogLog at ^NKG($agg, s, p, hll), hashed by SHA1 of the target's number; GraphIndex.EmptyHLL is the all-zero sketch. A rewrite (SweepEdges) makes each sketch again from the edges. Coverage (ontology-2): UpdateStructuralHLL, EmptyHLL.
A guess merges the sketches of the nodes reached, so it is not exact. The sketches have no graph part, so a guess mixes the edges of every graph.

GraphIndex.MergeHLL (the larger of each register) and GraphIndex.EstimateHLL (0.7182 m^2/Z, linear counting below 2.5 m); the caller is NKGAccelTraversal.CountDistinctKHop, the approx_count_distinct route. F-0819: in an all-graphs read the guess merged two graphs. Coverage (ontology-2): MergeHLL, EstimateHLL.
Taking an edge out of the interned snapshot drops both of its halves there and lowers the source's count. Its edge count and the source's sketch stay as they were.

GraphIndex.DeleteIndex (^NKG only): kills ^NKG(-1, s, p, o) and ^NKG(-2, o, p, s), steps ^NKG(-3, s) down and $meta version up; nothing when an end or the type has no number. $meta edgeCount stays (ADJ-T7.9.4), and so does the $agg sketch. Adjacency.Remove and RemoveSource call it only when no other graph holds the triple (ADJ-T3.3.2). Coverage (ontology-2): GraphIndex.DeleteIndex.
Before it writes an edge, the bulk edge load adds each end node the default graph lacks. An edge whose end node IRIS refuses is skipped and not counted.

EdgeScan.RegisterDefaultNode: one lookup per id per call (a seen set), then an INSERT into nodes with graph_id ''; a repeat (-119) counts as there; any other SQLCODE is answered, and BulkIngestEdgesSQL skips the edge without a word (WRT-B4.30, F-0307). The node half of the server loader calls it too, and raises on it. Coverage (ontology-2): RegisterDefaultNode.
The interned snapshot's count of nodes with edges is taken at each rewrite. Writes after that leave it as it was.

TraversalBuild.NKGLiveNodeCount answers $meta liveNodes, else nodeCount (the numbering high-water mark) for a snapshot no rewrite has counted; verify_sync reads it through Graph.KG.Traversal. Coverage (ontology-2): NKGLiveNodeCount.
A caller can make the engine forget the routes it keeps in memory: those of one graph and model, of one graph, or all of them.

invalidate_route_cache(graph_id, model_key, kind); kind None drops both the node and the edge route of a pair. erase_graph, erase_all, a restore, the vector upgrade and the registry updates of index state and recall call it (VEC-T2.13). Coverage (ontology-2): invalidate_route_cache.
The declared width of a table's vector column is read from IRIS's class records, else from its column list. No table, no declared width and a failed read all answer none.

GraphSchema.get_embedding_dimension: the LEN parameter of the emb property in %Dictionary.CompiledProperty, else the digits in INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS; every exception is swallowed. Setup, the vector tools, adoption and the upgrade read widths through it. Coverage (ontology-2): get_embedding_dimension.
The tools' statistics call gives a vector table's row count and the length of one sample value as its width. A failure comes back as an error entry and is not raised.

VectorOptimizer.get_vector_statistics(table_name='kg_NodeEmbeddings_optimized'), on the allow-list; an empty table answers an error entry too. It takes len() of the value the driver returns and does not parse text first, as validate_vector_table does (VEC-B11.29). Coverage (ontology-2): get_vector_statistics.
The web stats route's vector count is the count with no graph and no model. So it counts the whole legacy node table.
GET /stats on the Cypher HTTP server: embeddingCount is embedding_count() (VEC-B4.2); its node and edge counts are the default graph's (API-T8.8). Coverage (ontology-2): GET /stats.
The check for HNSW indexes on a table reads what IRIS holds now. If the read fails it answers none, and it notes the failure only for a caller that asks.

GraphSchema.hnsw_indexes: %Dictionary.CompiledIndex rows whose TypeClass holds HNSW; a user refused the dictionary in SQL is answered through Graph.KG.Meta.HnswIndexes when a native handle is given (OPS-T10.2). errors is the caller's list; without one a failure is only logged. Status, the index lists and the inventory use it. Coverage (ontology-2): hnsw_indexes.
The tools' call for tuning an HNSW index tests nothing. It always gives the same fixed advice.
VectorOptimizer.optimize_hnsw_parameters ignores its arguments and answers M 16 and efConstruction 200. Coverage (ontology-2): optimize_hnsw_parameters.

The nearest search of the engine's query part reads the route of one graph and model, the default graph when none is named. A query that is not numbers, or a failed read of the table, answers no rows and carries the error.

engine.cypher.execute_knn_vec (_CypherSubEngine.execute_knn_vec) hands the call to the store's execute_knn_vec: knn_route picks the table, and no route answers no rows; the error comes back in IVGResult.error. The label filter is read in the same graph, and TO_VECTOR takes the query's own width. Coverage (ontology-2): _CypherSubEngine.execute_knn_vec.
The web route for embedding works on the default graph only. It passes on a label filter and the force switch.

POST /admin/embed {label, force} calls embed_nodes(label=, force=) with no graph and no model key, so the default graph and the engine's own model; refused in read-only mode; any error is HTTP 500. Coverage (ontology-2): POST /admin/embed.
The waiting count covers the waiting entries of all graphs at once.

EmbedQueue.PendingCount counts the entries whose status reads PENDING, skipping $seq; embed_queue_pending and the background task (EmbedQueueTask.OnTask, before and after each pass) read it. Coverage (ontology-2): EmbedQueue.PendingCount.
The text and edge vector step first adds what placing needs, and last puts the new tables in place of the old ones. Each part can run again with no harm.

prepare_docs (a nullable graph_id on docs), prepare_edge_vectors (a staging table in the route shape and the two quarantine tables), finish_docs (docs rebuilt from the placed rows, keyed (graph_id, id), its indexes made again) and finish_edge_vectors (the source dropped and staging renamed over it), each through _run_tolerantly; migrate_docs_and_edge_vectors and the upgrade runner call them. Coverage (ontology-2): prepare_docs, finish_docs, prepare_edge_vectors, finish_edge_vectors.
Each part of the text and edge vector step can also hand back its SQL without running it.

docs_prepare_sql, docs_finish_sql, edge_vectors_prepare_sql (at a width and number type) and edge_vectors_finish_sql answer the bound statement lists of DOCS_PREPARE, DOCS_FINISH, EDGE_VECTORS_PREPARE and EDGE_VECTORS_FINISH. Coverage (ontology-2): docs_prepare_sql, docs_finish_sql, edge_vectors_prepare_sql, edge_vectors_finish_sql.
A new run refuses a staging or quarantine table for edge vectors that holds rows at another width. An empty one is made again at the new width.

prepare_edge_vectors through _reset_wrong_width_tables: the kg_EdgeEmbeddings staging table and edge_vector_quarantine, width from get_embedding_dimension; a RuntimeError names the table and both widths, else a warning and a DROP before the CREATE. Coverage (ontology-2): prepare_edge_vectors.
Each IVF or PLAID index can report its settings and its size. One that does not exist reports nothing.

IVFIndex.Info (nlist, dim, metric, indexed) and PLAIDSearch.Info (type, indexed, nlist, dim, totalTokens) answer {} for a missing name; ivf_info adds type ivf, plaid_info passes the answer on. indexed is the stored count, which can count an id twice or an erased graph's vectors (F-0608, F-0606). Coverage (ontology-2): IVFIndex.Info, PLAIDSearch.Info, ivf_info, plaid_info.
A tree index can report its settings and size too. One that does not exist reports as an empty index with the default settings.

VecIndex.Info: name, dim, metric, count, trees, leafSize; a missing name gives dim 0, metric cosine, count 0, trees 0 and leafSize 50. vec_info adds type vec. Coverage (ontology-2): VecIndex.Info, vec_info.
An IVF build writes its vectors in batches, each one into the group that was worked out for it. At the end, the build counts what the groups hold.

ivf_build: MiniBatchKMeans in Python, then IVFIndex.AddBatch per batch ({nodeId, cellIdx, vec} written to ^IVF(name, list, cell, id) with no width or repeat check) and IVFIndex.FinalizeIndex, which sets indexed to the number of (group, id) entries. Coverage (ontology-2): IVFIndex.AddBatch, IVFIndex.FinalizeIndex.
A tree index works out its measures on the server: cosine, straight line distance, sum of gaps, dot product and largest gap.

VecIndex.Cosine (0 when a vector has length 0), VecIndex.L2, VecIndex.L1, VecIndex.Dot and VecIndex.Chebyshev, all over $vectorop. Coverage (ontology-2): VecIndex.Cosine, VecIndex.L2, VecIndex.L1, VecIndex.Dot, VecIndex.Chebyshev.

A tree search ranks by distance, nearest first. For cosine the distance is one minus the cosine, and for dot it is minus the dot. For the other measures the score is the distance, so a lower score is closer.

VecIndex.Distance, used by BruteForceSearch and RankCandidates; an unknown measure falls back to cosine distance, which CheckMetric prevents (VEC-X11.20). TopK answers the cosine or the dot as the score, else the distance, and the distance as well. Coverage (ontology-2): VecIndex.Distance.
A score helper gives the cosine or the dot as it is, and one over one plus the distance for the other measures. No search calls it.
VecIndex.Similarity; no caller in the product at the pin. Coverage (ontology-2): VecIndex.Similarity.
A tree index can store a matrix and work out one more measure from it. No build and no search uses that measure.

VecIndex.SetInverseCov writes one row of an inverse covariance at ^VecIdx(name, cfg, invCov, row); VecIndex.Mahalanobis reads it. Create refuses the mahalanobis measure (VEC-X11.20). Coverage (ontology-2): VecIndex.Mahalanobis, VecIndex.SetInverseCov.
The types those resolvers return are not served either. So their fields never run.

api/gql/types.py (the property accessor of its Node; the relation fields of its Protein, Gene and Pathway types) is imported only by api/gql/resolvers/query.py, api/gql/resolvers/mutation.py and unit tests. The served schema takes its node types from api/gql/core/types.py and the biomedical types from examples/domains/biomedical/types.py. Coverage (ontology-2): the fields of api/gql/types.py.
The loaders in the api core folder are not used either. The app builds other loaders, which read the tables directly.

GenericNodeLoader, PropertyLoader and LabelLoader of api/gql/core/loaders.py read through engine.get_nodes; no app builds them. examples/domains/biomedical/loaders.py imports two of them and never calls them. build_graphql_context builds the loaders of api/gql/loaders.py over the shared connection (API-B6.6). Coverage (ontology-2): the three batch loaders of api/gql/core/loaders.py.
The create protein call writes a new protein node in the default graph. When it carries a vector, it stores that too.

createProtein (api/gql/schema.py:253-262) calls BiomedicalDomainResolver._create_protein_mutation, which builds a new IRISGraphEngine over the shared connection: create_node(id, labels Protein, name, function, organism) and store_embedding with no graph, then commits the shared connection. create_node commits on its own, so a failed store_embedding leaves the node without its vector. Read-only mode refuses it first (API-X6.8). The integration tests run the served schema and need live IRIS. Coverage (ontology-2): createProtein.
The create protein call refuses an id that the default graph holds already. It also refuses a vector that is not 768 wide. Nothing is written then.

Both checks run before create_node: the width check first, then engine.node_exists(id), which asks the default graph only. A node of the same id in a named graph does not stop it. Both refusals are GraphQL errors (plain Exception). Coverage (ontology-2): createProtein refusals.
The delete protein call removes the node with that id from the default graph, whatever its labels.

deleteProtein (api/gql/schema.py:275-284) calls BiomedicalDomainResolver._delete_protein_mutation: engine.delete_node(id) with the graph omitted, which removes the node with its labels, properties, vectors and edges in one eraser transaction, then commits the shared connection and clears the protein loader's entry. No label check. Read-only mode refuses it first (API-X6.8). Coverage (ontology-2): deleteProtein.
The delete protein call refuses an id that the default graph does not hold. It also refuses when another graph holds the same id. Nothing is removed then.

node_exists asks the default graph (not found otherwise); delete_node with the graph omitted raises ValueError, before anything is deleted, when more than one graph holds the id. Both are GraphQL errors. Coverage (ontology-2): deleteProtein refusals.
The domain hooks never run in the app. No app registers a domain or puts one in the context.

The hooks of DomainResolver, CompositeDomainResolver and BiomedicalDomainResolver (register a domain, resolve a node to a domain type, list query and mutation fields) have no caller in a served app: _load_node asks for a domain_resolver the context never holds (API-T6.12), and the served protein, gene and pathway fields and the mutations call the resolver's private methods directly. Coverage (ontology-2): the domain resolver hooks.
The property field of a node answers one property by its key. It reads nothing more from IRIS.

The field of the core Node interface returns properties.get(key), else null; GenericNode and the biomedical types inherit it, so the value is what node, nodes or the loaders already read (API-B6.6 for the biomedical types). Coverage (ontology-2): the property field of the core Node interface.
No served field returns an edge. So the edge type and its qualifier field never run.

Edge (with Edge.qualifier) is imported by api/gql/core/resolvers.py and named by no field type; the schema lists only GenericNode as an extra type, so Edge is not in the served schema. Coverage (ontology-2): Edge.qualifier.
A GraphQL call never closes the app's connection when it ends. The connection stays open for the next call.

DatabaseConnectionExtension.on_request_end closes db_connection only when the context says owns_connection; build_graphql_context always sets it False, as both app factories use it. Coverage (ontology-2): on_request_end.
After any failure, the server drops its engine and runs the query once more. So a write may run twice.

_run_cypher makes two attempts under _engine_lock: any exception on the first, a parse error included, runs _reset_engine (which closes the cached engine's connection) and retries on a new engine; the second failure is raised (API-T8.5.3). A failure reported in result.error is raised after the loop and not retried. Serves /api/cypher, /db/neo4j/tx/commit and /db/{db}/query/v2. Whether it should retry is HD-1603 (API-Q8.5.2). Coverage (ontology-2): _run_cypher.
Inside IRIS the server can run as a WSGI app. That works only when the operator has added the package that wraps it.

wsgi_app is a2wsgi.ASGIMiddleware(app) when a2wsgi imports, else None; no dependency list of pyproject.toml names a2wsgi. A WSGI host carries no web socket, so the Bolt web socket route cannot answer there; whether a2wsgi runs the lifespan (the TCP Bolt listener) is outside the pin and not checked. Coverage (ontology-2): wsgi_app.
The browser route serves the graph browser only when its files sit beside the package. The built package leaves them out, so the route then answers a page that says so.

_BROWSER_DIR is iris_vector_graph/browser_static: when it exists it is mounted at /browser (html=True) and GET /browser redirects to /browser/; else GET /browser answers 200 'Graph Browser not installed' with install hints. The wheel excludes browser_static; the source tree and the sdist hold it. The key gate covers it (API-T8.11). Coverage (ontology-2): browser_redirect and the /browser mount.
A Bolt session does not close the IRIS connection it opened. The connection stays open after the driver has gone.

The session builds its engine (_make_engine, a new connection) on its first RUN and keeps it in self._engine; the finally blocks of BoltSession.run and TcpBoltSession.run close only the socket, never self._engine.conn, after GOODBYE, a dropped socket or a failed handshake alike. A session that never runs a query opens none. Coverage (ontology-2): the Bolt session's IRIS connection lifecycle.
A discard drops the rows that wait for a pull and answers success.

TAG_DISCARD clears _pending_result and _pending_columns, answers SUCCESS {type: r} with no has_more and sets READY; its n and qid fields are not read. With nothing waiting it changes nothing. Before login it is refused (API-X9.3); in FAILED it is IGNORED (API-T9.9). Coverage (ontology-2): TAG_DISCARD.
A logoff ends the login and answers success. The session may log on again with the key.

TAG_LOGOFF sets _authenticated False and answers SUCCESS {}; it is one of the messages allowed before login. With the key set, the session then runs nothing until a LOGON or HELLO shows the key again (API-X9.3, API-X9.4); with no key set nothing checks the flag. Rows still waiting stay. Coverage (ontology-2): TAG_LOGOFF.
A pull with no rows waiting answers success at once, with no rows.

_handle_pull with _pending_result None answers SUCCESS {type: r} and sets READY: a PULL after BEGIN, COMMIT, ROLLBACK, DISCARD or an earlier PULL. Coverage (ontology-2): TAG_PULL with nothing pending.
A new run drops any rows that the last run left waiting.

_handle_run sets _pending_result to the new rows (bolt_server.py:608) and answers qid 0: one result waits at a time, in or out of a transaction. A refused or failed run sets it to None. Coverage (ontology-2): TAG_RUN while rows wait.
Started straight from Python, the web app takes calls on every network address, on port 8000. Its TCP listener binds every address too, unless an operator sets one.

python -m iris_vector_graph.cypher_api runs uvicorn.run(app, host 0.0.0.0, port 8000). The lifespan starts the Bolt listener on BOLT_TCP_HOST (default 0.0.0.0) and BOLT_TCP_PORT (default 7687) unless BOLT_ENABLED is 0, false or no; a port in use is only logged. Any start but ivg server start, uvicorn --host 127.0.0.1 included, leaves Bolt on every address (API-T9.1 for the command). Coverage (ontology-2): the __main__ entry and _lifespan.
The properties field of a node always answers an empty list. Each property comes as its own field of the label's type.

Node.properties returns [] and every generated type inherits it; map_node_data passes each property as a string keyword to the label's type instead (the type has a field per key sampled at start, emb, vector and embedding excluded; reserved names get a p_ prefix). tests/e2e/test_gql_node_queries.py asks for properties and does not check them. Coverage (ontology-2): Node.properties.
A column name that must go into SQL is put in double quotes. Any quote inside it is doubled, so it stays one name.
quote_identifier; used for the result column aliases the SQL store builds (iris_sql_store.py:413, 421, 530). Coverage (ontology-2): quote_identifier.
The page, design and scenario routes answer fixed pages and forms. The bio and FHIR pages also show counts read from their graph.

GET /, /arch/fraud, /arch/bio, /arch/fhir, /fraud, /bio, /api/fraud/scenario/{n}, /api/bio/scenario/{n} and /api/fhir/scenario/{n} build HTML from constants (an unknown scenario answers a message, 404 on the FHIR one). /bio shows the node and edge counts of bio:demo (offline on error); /api/fhir/stats shows the registered FHIR graph's status and label counts, or 503 with the error text on failure. The live panel lists the first 40 cohort patients from the seed data, not from IRIS. Coverage (ontology-2): homepage, demo_card, arch_fraud, arch_bio, arch_fhir, fraud_page, bio_page, the scenario routes, stats_cards, search_form, live_panel.
The fraud demo asks the fraud server for a score. In demo mode, or when that call fails, it scores by the amount alone.

POST /api/fraud/score validates the form (FraudTransactionQuery), then FraudAPIClient.score_transaction POSTs FRAUD_API_URL (default http://localhost:8100) /fraud/score in MLP mode with FRAUD_API_KEY. Any error counts a failure; after five the CircuitBreaker opens for 60 s, then lets one call try. The heuristic: over 10000 gives 0.85, over 5000 0.65, over 2000 0.35, else 0.15. scoring_mode words the source for the status card. The fraud server's own default port is 8000 (API-T13.5). A bad form answers the error text with 200. Coverage (ontology-2): get_fraud_client, scoring_mode, score_transaction, CircuitBreaker.is_open, record_success, record_failure.
The graph and the audit trail that the fraud demo draws are made up. They are not read from IRIS.

The payer, device, merchant and address of the form plus fixed txn_hist, dev and merch nodes, and audit entries with fixed dates; the landing card calls them the payer's device and merchant graph and the bitemporal audit trail behind the score. Coverage (ontology-2): the fraud demo's result view.
The protein search matches text in the bio demo's graph, not vectors. A name search ranks the exact symbol first. Any other kind matches words in the protein's note.

POST /api/bio/search: ProteinSearchQuery (text, kind name, sequence or function, top_k 1-50). By name: symbol or name LIKE the text, upper case, scored 1.0 for the exact symbol and 0.8 otherwise. Sequence and function both score term_score, the share of query words found in the annotation. Every read names graph_id bio:demo in Graph_KG.rdf_props; ids show as symbols (protein:TP53 shows TP53). Coverage (ontology-2): search_proteins, term_score, the bio search route.
The network and path routes walk the bio demo's links in both directions. A path is a shortest one within the hop cap, five at most.

GET /api/bio/network/{id}: get_interaction_network refuses a protein bio:demo lacks, then grows rings of interaction edges either way for expand_depth rounds (no upper bound but 500 nodes). POST /api/bio/pathway: PathwayQuery max_hops 1-5; find_pathway runs an undirected breadth-first search and refuses when none is found; confidence is the mean of the hops' confidence qualifiers. Coverage (ontology-2): get_interaction_network, find_pathway, the network and path routes.
When IRIS cannot be reached, a bio or FHIR route answers the error text instead of a result.

The bio routes answer {error: text} or an error block with status 200; the FHIR routes answer 503 with the text (the FHIR page shows it in place of the counts). The fraud demo falls back instead (API-T13.91). Coverage (ontology-2): the demo routes' error answers.
The bio seed loads the bio demo's graph. It first erases that graph, unless the graph already holds as many nodes and edges as the seed.

python -m iris_demo_server.services.bio_demo_data connects with IVG_BIO_* then IVG_FHIR_* (defaults localhost, 31972, IVGFHIR, _SYSTEM/SYS). It compares the bio:demo counts of Graph_KG.nodes and rdf_edges with the seed's; when they differ it runs engine.erase_graph on bio:demo, then create_node and create_edge (the interaction predicate, qualifiers type and confidence) in bio:demo, each its own transaction, and raises when the counts then differ. Other content of the same counts is left alone. Coverage (ontology-2): bio_demo_data seed, build_graph, its connection settings and engine, the __main__ entry.
The FHIR seed writes about two hundred made up patients and their visits, each with a fixed id. So a rerun rewrites the same set.

python -m iris_demo_server.services.fhir_demo_data: build_cohort (random seed 231) gives the organisations, practitioners, 200 patients, encounters, ICD-10 conditions and LOINC labs, each PUT with its fixed id through IVGDemo.FHIRLoad.Dispatch after fhir_graph_register of the endpoint. A PUT that does not answer 20x raises. Coverage (ontology-2): fhir_demo_data seed, main, build_cohort, the __main__ entry.
Before it writes, the FHIR seed deletes the conditions that the live panel added. After, it adds the demo concepts and runs a sync until no change waits, fifty tries at most.

remove_live_conditions DELETEs every live Condition (id prefix demo-live-) found in the package's Rsrc table; load_concepts runs create_node and create_edge (narrower) in concepts:demo and code_crosswalk_add, with no erase first; sync_until_done calls fhir_graph_sync until it is not busy and nothing is pending, 0.2 s apart, and returns the last reply after 50 tries. Coverage (ontology-2): remove_live_conditions, load_concepts, sync_until_done.
The FHIR seed also compiles the demo's own class into the namespace. With a flag, it compiles every product class too and sets up the schema.

load_classes writes each .cls under the root to /tmp/ivgdemo-<namespace>/ on the IRIS side and loads it with %SYSTEM.OBJ.Load flags ck-d, over the Native API, returning the error texts (the seed raises on any). The demo class is IVGDemo.FHIRLoad; --deploy-ivg also loads iris_src/src and runs initialize_schema with auto_deploy_objectscript False. Coverage (ontology-2): load_classes, the FHIR seed's connection settings and engine.
A demo class inside IRIS runs one FHIR call with no web layer in front. A write through it lands as one over the web would.

IVGDemo.FHIRLoad.Dispatch(endpoint, method, path, body) builds an HS.FHIRServer.API.Data.Request and calls HS.FHIRServer.Service.DispatchRequest: any method and path, no key, as the calling IRIS user. It answers {status, body}, or {status: error, error} when the endpoint is unknown or the service throws. Only the FHIR seed compiles it; initialize_schema does not. make_dispatch calls it over the Native API. Coverage (ontology-2): IVGDemo.FHIRLoad.Dispatch, make_dispatch.
The FHIR search expands known demo concepts by up to three hops. It then ranks the patients and clinicians linked to them.

parse_search refuses (400) no concept, an unknown one, hops outside 0-3 and evidence other than diagnoses or all. FHIRGraphDemoClient.search: fhir_expand_concepts over concepts:demo (narrower, out), fhir_resolve_concepts in the registered FHIR graph (exact and narrower, or every relation), kg_PERSONALIZED_PAGERANK (0.85, 20 rounds, both directions) in that graph; top 10 patients with a matching code, 5 near ones and 5 clinicians; names and codes read live from the Rsrc table (display_name). Coverage (ontology-2): parse_search, results_view, the FHIR search route.
The neighbourhood route shows what links to one key in that graph, one step out. It refuses a key of the wrong shape.

GET /api/fhir/neighborhood/{key}: a key not matching Type/id answers 400. The edges where the key is either end in the registered FHIR graph, plus the out edges of the encounters, conditions and observations among them; at most 80 nodes, labelled from the Rsrc table; 503 with the error text on failure. Coverage (ontology-2): FHIRGraphDemoClient.neighborhood and its route.
The live add writes one condition per patient and code. Adding the same pair again rewrites that condition.

add_condition PUTs Condition/demo-live-<patient>-<code without dots>, onset today, through IVGDemo.FHIRLoad.Dispatch; the graph sees it at the next sync, which /api/fhir/live/sync runs. The route checks the Patient key shape and that the code is one of the demo's ICD-10 codes (400), and needs no key (API-B13.2). Coverage (ontology-2): add_condition, live_condition_id, condition.
No demo route keeps a session or builds a score from a bare number. That model code never runs.
DemoSession.add_query, switch_mode and is_expired and FraudScoringResult.from_probability have no caller; no module imports models/session.py. Coverage (ontology-2): those four methods.
The fraud server scores a payment from the payer's events of the last day and week. A model it loads at start makes the score.

POST /fraud/score in MLP mode: compute_features counts the payer's gs_events rows and their amounts in 24 h and distinct devices in 7 days (risk_neighbors_1hop is always 0); get_node_embedding gives zeros (API-B13.7); eight features and 768 numbers go to the TorchScript model of FRAUD_MODEL_PATH (default /models/fraud_mlp.torchscript); sigmoid gives prob. generate_reasons gives 3 to 5 reasons; the likeness reason needs the centroid, which load_fraud_centroid reads with fetchone on an iris.sql.exec result and else leaves None. A failure answers 500 with its text. Coverage (ontology-2): score_mlp_mode, compute_features, generate_reasons, load_torchscript_model, load_fraud_centroid, the score route.
The fraud server refuses the subgraph mode. It answers that the mode is not built.
mode EGO answers 501 'EGO mode not implemented in MVP'; any other mode is refused by the request model (422). Coverage (ontology-2): the score route's EGO branch.
With no model file at start, the fraud server scores with a stand-in model of random weights.

FileNotFoundError at startup loads create_dummy_model: a traced torch Linear(776, 1) with its random start weights, new at each start; the docstring's 'about 0.1' is not enforced.
